title: Show the move tip once, not on every uproot forever
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (60)', first entry, with the measurement from cycle 60 as its justification.

The armed prompt now teaches the move preview, and it costs 185px of the message row's 306px of headroom -- on EVERY uproot, forever, to teach something once. cmd budgets reports 755 of 876 px, state 'tight', 121px clear of the 40px floor declared at game/game.gd:1883. It passes; it is still a poor trade.

RunConfig's milestone set (MILESTONE_PREFIX, game/run_config.gd:91) is already a persisted seen-once mechanism, so this needs NO save-version bump -- which is what makes it cheap enough to be worth doing rather than tolerating.

Show the tip the first time an uproot window opens; drop back to the short warning afterwards. That returns 185px to the row AND makes the hint more likely to be read, since a message that appears once is not wallpaper.

ACCEPTANCE: the tip appears once per save; cmd budgets returns to roughly 570px; a test drives first-time and subsequent arms.
close_reason: Tip shown once via RunConfig's milestone set (no SAVE_VERSION bump; verified invisible in the notebook, which is TABLE-driven). NOTE: the acceptance criterion I wrote was wrong -- cmd budgets stays at 755/tight, correctly, because the corpus prices both forms and the budget measures the ceiling the format allows, not frequency. 0eb443c

title: Tell the player the move tool exists
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (59)', first entry. PLAYER-FACING, and the highest-value item in the queue right now because the feature is already built.

Arming an uproot and hovering a destination shows cost and gain together (cycle 59). Nothing hints that this is possible. The only signal is a button reading 'Really uproot? (+N)' (game/hud.gd:1206), which asks the player to confirm a DELETION -- it does not invite them to go looking at other cells.

So a complete tool is sitting behind a prompt that says the opposite of what it does. Either a few words in that button, or a one-shot message the first time a window opens.

BLOCKED-ISH on width, like -eupm: 'Really uproot? (+99)' is already the longest state that button takes, and the selection panel has no slack (-r722). Measure first. The one-shot message route avoids the width problem entirely and goes through Hud.message_corpus(), which is budgeted.

ACCEPTANCE: a first-time player discovers the move preview without being told; the new string is measured against its box or added to the message corpus.
close_reason: The armed prompt now points at the move preview: 'Hover to compare a new spot.' Deliberately a comparison and not a promise to move, since -h5w6 is undecided. Costs 185px of the message row's headroom, leaving 121 against a 40px floor -- state 'tight', which is the argument for the one-shot follow-up.

title: Write the run.json schema down where /verify can see it
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's step 4, gap [G-058], filed upstream as gh#46.

I passed Phase 4 evidence to verify_ledger record under a key named `phase4`. It was accepted without comment, dropped, and then reported as missing ('warranted with no Phase 4 checks recorded'). The real key is `checks`, with name/result entries. `tier`, `phases` and `notes` were dropped the same way.

The upstream fix is gh#46 (warn on unknown keys). The IN-PROJECT half is cheaper and does not wait on a release: write the schema into .claude/skills/verify-bd-item/, which already carries the ledger-before-commit rule, with a filled-in example. Recovering the shape by reading verify_ledger.py is what this cycle did, and it is not repeatable knowledge until it is written down.

ACCEPTANCE: verify-bd-item carries a correct run.json example; a row recorded from it reports no 'no Phase 4 checks' warning.
notes: SECOND SIGHTING, cycle 69 (not a duplicate filing -- this bead already covers it). This time it cost a wrong row rather than a warning: lint_exit / tests_exit / tests_total / tests_failed / assertions were all accepted silently and the row came out 'verdict': 'unknown', 'lint': None, 'tests': None. The real shape is nested (lint: {new:...}, tests: {failed:...}) plus a top-level verdict, and none of it is in --help. Note also that upstream gh#46 is CLOSED and fixed at 0.47.0 (difflib suggestion on unknown keys, templates/tools/verify_ledger.py:1101-1107) -- this project pins 0.38.0 on purpose (gh#43, bead -ny3h), so writing the schema down locally is the fix available here. Raised to P1: it has now silently corrupted the evidence file twice.
close_reason: Shipped as tools/run_json_check.py rather than a document: the key set is derived from every run.get() in the installed verify_ledger, so a harness upgrade updates it for free. Found 'tier' on its first run -- a key I had written into every run.json this session and which is read nowhere. 769e045

title: Build scope-vs-claim: does a check's stated scope match its actual scope
description:
SOURCE: step 0's second pre-flight item. SECOND INDEPENDENT IDENTIFICATION, which is this project's build-it bar -- filed at P1 so it does not get named a third time.

First (cycle 49, log.md): 'budget-corpus-audit' -- _budget_hud_message_row's evidence string said 'over every plant name and corn level' and was true when written, false for seven cycles after, while the budget reported green over a subset of its row.

Second (cycle 50): three of four cardinal-facing cases were covered by tests BY ACCIDENT (+X in the gait test, -X via the corpse test, +Y used without its value asserted) and the fourth by nothing. Nothing in the suite's own descriptions gave any way to see the gap.

Third, same shape, already fixed: mirror_check compared a block it had silently truncated, and suite_reach_check's autoload map returned empty without saying so.

The general question is bigger than budgets and bigger than checkers: **a check states a scope in prose and covers a scope in code, and nothing compares the two.** That is why the failure is always silent -- the description is what a reader trusts and it is the half that cannot fail.

The skill should carry the recognition patterns (a free-text evidence/corpus string; a region delimited by a marker; a set of cases enumerated by hand; a denominator that can be zero for two different reasons) and the cheap test for each: name the scope out loud, then ask what else falls inside it. Cross-reference derive-the-list, which handles the case where the set IS derivable, and house-static-checker's denominator rules.

ACCEPTANCE: .claude/skills/scope-vs-claim/SKILL.md exists and cites all three incidents above as its evidence, with the file:line for each.
close_reason: Built .claude/skills/scope-vs-claim/SKILL.md citing all four incidents with file:line.

title: Build the verify-bd-item skill, identified twice and never built
description:
SOURCE: step 0's second pre-flight item (skill ideas in log.md vs .claude/skills/).

log.md:3115 names it, log.md:3201 opens with 'Same as last cycle: a verify-bd-item loop skill. Ran the identical fifteen-step sequence five more times.' Two explicit identifications, absent from .claude/skills/. CLAUDE.md step 0: 'Two independent identifications of the same missing skill means build it -- do not identify it a third time.'

It is not hypothetical any more. Cycle 48 ran that sequence by hand and dropped a step: the verify ledger row was recorded AFTER the commit, so reach came back 0/0 and the row carries no evidence for its own 'warranted' verdict. That is the exact failure the original identification predicted ('every one is a place to silently drop a step').

The skill should carry the ORDER and the traps, not just the list: ledger row before the commit (reach is computed from the diff); take a suite count on both sides of a rename or dependency change; read the denominators not the exit code; gap-id scan before appending to log-devtools.md; never rewrite a ledger row to look better.

ACCEPTANCE: the skill exists, names the ordering constraint that broke cycle 48, and is written so following it produces a ledger row with non-zero reach.
close_reason: Built .claude/skills/verify-bd-item/SKILL.md, leading with the ordering constraints rather than the step list. 2e8993d

title: Pests have no idle animation, only plants do
description: The second half of James's 'animate all the plants and enemies' ask. Plant._wobble_time now drives an idle sway for every placed plant (plant-tower-defense-04x), but Pest has no equivalent - a walking aphid or beetle is a static sprite sliding along the road, and the new facing rotation (129) made that more visible, not less. A fifth plant: seed-puff attack animation where the dandelion visibly loses fluff as it fires, and seeds that ARC and DETONATE rather than travelling straight like a Corn Cobbler kernel or landing instantly like a Chomp bite. Add real additional waves to the table, and at least one boss pest: bigger health pool, a distinct sprite, and a mechanic that is NOT just 'armoured but more'. title: Four tests write the developer's real user://highscore.save
description: test_selftest.gd:679 (test_run_config_high_score_only_ever_goes_up), :1014, :4326 and :4921 (test_a_record_set_by_quitting_is_announced_on_the_title_screen) all set RunConfig.campaign_high_score/endless_high_score in memory and then call RunConfig.record_score(), while RunConfig.save_path is still the REAL user://highscore.save. record_score() calls _save(), so each headless suite run rewrites the developer's own save with whatever number the test just staged. Observed over two runs of the full suite on 2026-08-16: the file went v5/308/5008 -> v6/310/5010 -> v6/2/2. Both high scores were destroyed; only a scratchpad copy taken before the work brought them back. These tests stash and restore the in-memory scores, which is what makes it invisible -- the FILE keeps the last number written. Fix: give each of them the scratch-save redirect test_economy._with_scratch_save already implements (RunConfig.save_path = a user://test_*.save, restore and delete afterwards), or add the same wrapper to test_selftest.gd. Related: harness issue #33 (--isolated isolates the bus, not user://), which makes this worse under two concurrent agents.
close_reason: Fixed: four tests redirected to scratch paths (three named in the bead plus a fourth in test_economy.gd found by the new guard), scores restored as well as save_path, and test_no_test_persists_through_the_players_own_save added as a comment-stripping source guard. Real save verified byte-identical across two full suite runs.

title: Sweep test/ for other group reads taken by index
description: test_kernels_launch read kernels[0] from a tree-global group and measured a leaked object every run - green for months, red the moment four unrelated tests were appended. Nothing enumerates the other group reads (pests, husks, kernels, plants); any taken by index has the same defect. A sweep for get_nodes_in_group(...)[0] in test/ finds the rest in one pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: A damaged plant's health bar eats clicks on the playfield
description: Plant._health_back and _health_bar are ColorRects with the default MOUSE_FILTER_STOP, parked over the playfield. A damaged plant therefore has a 32x5 strip that swallows clicks meant for the board. Pre-existing; found while adding the health bar notches.
close_reason: Closed

title: Post-mortem calls your best chokepoint your weakest ground
description: Game._note_lane_loss is called from _on_pest_died (every kill, at the pest's position) as well as _on_pest_escaped. So _run_losses counts kills, not damage. That is correct for LanePressureOverlay, whose doc says 'how far did pests get' - a kill at cell 30 of 40 IS pressure. But run_summary.gd:201 _worst_cell_text() labels the highest-count cell 'Weakest ground - N lost there', so a well-defended chokepoint is reported to the player as their weakest ground, every run. The advice is not just useless, it is inverted. Found by the agent building the prep depth readout, which declined to reuse worst_run_cell() for exactly this reason.
close_reason: Closed

title: A truncated save silently zeroes a high score that can never be restored
description: RunConfig._save stamps a SAVE_VERSION line on every write and _load tests only begins_with('v') -- the version is written and never actually read, so a future format change has no migration hook despite the field existing to provide one. Worse, int('') is 0 in GDScript, so a truncated or partially-written save loads as a zero high score, and record_score only ever raises a record: once it reads 0 the real number is gone forever with no way back. A save file is the one thing in this project the player cannot regenerate by playing.
acceptance_criteria: A malformed, truncated or short save leaves the existing in-memory scores untouched rather than zeroing them, and the version field is actually consulted. Unit tests cover a truncated file, a garbage file, and a future version number.
close_reason: Closed

title: Quitting an endless run through pause files no score
description: RunConfig.record_score has exactly one caller, Game._end_run, reached only from the victory branch or from lives hitting 0. has_more_waves() is unconditionally true in endless, so victory is unreachable there -- meaning the ONLY way to bank an endless score is to lose. Cycle 8's pause screen then added two exits that bypass _end_run entirely: RestartButton calls reload_current_scene and GateButton calls change_scene_to_file. So a player who quits a long endless run voluntarily files nothing, and the run they were most likely to be proud of is the one guaranteed not to count.
acceptance_criteria: Leaving a run through any exit files the score exactly once, and a re-entry cannot file it twice. Unit test covers quitting via both pause exits.
close_reason: Closed

title: Uproot-as-score: refunds credit seeds_earned_total, so plant-uproot cycling inflates the high score
description: SeedBank.refund routes through add_seeds, which increments seeds_earned_total -- the number both per-mode high scores are kept on. So planting a Corn for 10 and uprooting it for 6 costs 4 seeds of wallet and CREDITS 6 to the recorded score, repeatably. A 100-seed float converts to roughly +150 score with no gameplay at all. Scaling the refund by health in cycle 7 killed uproot-as-repair and left this untouched; the seed_bank comment 'Refunds count too' documents the behaviour as deliberate, but it predates high scores being a scoreboard players compete on.
acceptance_criteria: Uprooting cannot raise seeds_earned_total. A unit test plants and uproots in a loop and asserts the recorded score does not move, while ordinary income still counts.
close_reason: Closed

title: Common seed packets silently become rare ones once Chomp unlocks
description: SeedBank._roll_packet filters the locked pool to ids at or below the packet's max_tier, then falls back to the WHOLE locked pool when that filtered pool is empty. Chomp is tier 1 and Sunflower is tier 2, so the moment Chomp unlocks the filtered pool for a common packet is always empty and a 20-seed common packet can hand out the tier-2 Sunflower. That makes the two packet tiers indistinguishable in the only way they were supposed to differ, and both tooltips become false: the common button says 'tier 1 only' and the rare one says 'the only reliable way to a Seed Sunflower'.
acceptance_criteria: A common packet can never yield a plant above its max_tier. When nothing at or below that tier remains locked, the purchase is refused with a reason rather than silently upgraded, and the tooltips match the behaviour. Unit test covers the exhausted-pool case.
close_reason: Common packets refuse rather than falling back to the whole locked pool; no charge on refusal, no soft-lock possible. Fixed a pre-existing test that was green only because of the bug.
