title: Give the boss a body, since it already has a mechanic
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'Requested directly by James', second bullet, after the cycle-76 audit. PLAYER-FACING, and it is the narrow half of an ask that read as entirely unbuilt for many cycles.

The ask was: at least one boss pest -- bigger health pool, a distinct sprite, a mechanic that isn't just 'armoured but more'.

The MECHANIC shipped. WaveDirector.wave_carries_boss() (game/wave_director.gd:319) feeds the HUD prep note, and game/game.gd:796 documents it: a pest whose species names a split bursts into that many when killed. That is not 'armoured but more' and it is the interesting third of the ask.

The BODY did not. game/game.gd:767 says it outright -- a pest that arrives because a boss burst is the same object. So the boss has no health pool of its own and no sprite of its own, and a player meets it as an ordinary pest that happens to explode into others.

Two constraints already on the board. Pest declares exactly two species (game/pest.gd:16-17) so a third is a real addition rather than a flag. And a corpse currently lingers a flat DEATH_LINGER for every pest (game/pest.gd:200) -- see -rowt, which wants that scaled by difficulty; a boss is the case that makes that bead obviously right.

ACCEPTANCE: a boss is distinguishable from an aphid before it dies, without reading a health bar; its health is its own number rather than a mutation multiplier; the split mechanic still works unchanged.

title: Compute the row ceilings the other three surfaces write in comments
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (75)', first entry. Enumerated over every row-limited surface in the game, not sampled.

TitleScreen.menu_capacity() (game/title_screen.gd:169-174) COMPUTES its ceiling: it walks hint_y(n+1) + HINT_HEIGHT against the backdrop horizon and returns the count, so adding a destination moves the number on its own.

The other three write the arithmetic in prose and pin it with a test:
  - OptionsScreen, game/options_screen.gd:100-108 -- three rows from 256 at 48 foot at 392, footer at 440, gap 48 against OverlayScreen.FOOTER_GAP of 24
  - the milestone shelf, game/notebook_screen.gd:166-168 -- SHELF_ROW_PITCH 42 x 7 + 3 = 297 against a 300px box
  - RunSummary, game/run_summary.gd:77 -- rows step 38, the seventh foots at 448, BUTTON_Y is 476, an eighth would foot at 486

All three are correct and tested. All three were derived by hand, in three files, by three cycles that could not see each other, and each has to be re-derived by the next person who wants a row. The fourth shows the shape that does not rot and it is the OLDEST of them.

Blocks -1490 (the options panel decision) and the seeds row idea, both of which are 'this surface is full' problems wearing different hats.

Do not force one helper if the four shapes genuinely differ -- two of them measure to a footer and two to a box, and a helper that needs four arguments to express that is worse than four computations. The deliverable is that each surface COMPUTES its ceiling, shared or not.

ACCEPTANCE: adding a row to any of the three fails or fits without anyone re-deriving arithmetic from a comment; the existing tests still pin the result rather than being replaced by the computation.

title: Run the parallel-safe gates from one command that derives its own list
description:
SOURCE: log-devtools.md and CLAUDE.md step 5, cycle 75.

CLAUDE.md carries a hand-maintained list of ten stdlib checkers in tools/. Every cycle for the last several I have retyped that list into a shell for-loop to run them, which is a per-cycle transcription of a list that already exists in prose -- the same disease the workflow cured for the work queue when it made bd the only place items live.

Two consequences, both real. A new tools/*_check.py that nobody adds to the CLAUDE.md block is invisible and never runs; and the loop I retype can silently omit one, which no exit code catches because the omitted checker never reports anything.

Shape: tools/check_all.py, deriving its list from glob('tools/*_check.py') rather than from the prose block, running each, and printing a denominator -- 'ran 10 of 10 discovered'. Note the two exclusions it must handle deliberately rather than by accident: mirror_check --fix WRITES AGENTS.md so the runner must call it read-only, and run_json_check exits 2 when there is no run.json, which is the normal state at the start of a cycle and must not read as a failure.

Then CLAUDE.md's block becomes a description of what the command finds rather than the list itself, and step 2 can name one command.

ACCEPTANCE: one command runs every parallel-safe checker; adding a new tools/*_check.py makes it run without editing any list; the denominator is printed and a checker that could not run is named rather than skipped.

title: Decide how the options panel grows before a feature needs it to
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (74)', third entry. Blocks -u9uh.

OptionsScreen.PANEL (game/options_screen.gd:109) is sized from the row count on purpose and its header does the arithmetic: three rows from ROWS_TOP 256 at ROW_HEIGHT 48 put the last button foot at 392 against a footer starting at 440, so the gap is 48. OverlayScreen.FOOTER_GAP is 24 (game/overlay_screen.gd:92). A FOURTH row puts the foot at exactly 440 -- gap 0 -- and trips the rule.

That is the good kind of wall. It also means every future option is a panel-geometry decision before it is anything else, and the milestone shelf taught this project that picking the way out while holding a feature is the expensive order.

Two candidate answers, both already precedented here. Grow PANEL and re-derive the arithmetic in its header, which is what the header is for. Or split audio onto its own screen the way Keys already is, which the title screen has room for only if a destination name fits 146px (see the cycle-64 entry on that).

Note PANEL is a hard-coded Rect2 with a comment saying it was DERIVED -- a recorded value with no equality assertion behind it, which is exactly the shape derive-the-list warns about. Whatever is decided, consider computing it.

ACCEPTANCE: a fourth option can be added without anyone re-deriving panel geometry in the moment; the decision and its reason are written where the next person adding an option will read them.

title: Make sound a dial, not just a switch
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (74)', first entry. PLAYER-FACING.

OptionsScreen.OPTIONS (game/options_screen.gd:83-99) is three rows and every one is an On/Off flip (:265, ON_TEXT/OFF_TEXT at :123-124). AudioServer appears NOWHERE in game/, so there are no buses and never have been. Music sits at a fixed BASE_VOLUME_DB of -14.0 (game/music.gd:53) and effects default to 0.0. A player who finds the music loud has exactly one option and it is silence.

Cycle 74 made this cheap by accident. Sfx.tune_voice is now the single place every voice property is written, and Music._start (game/music.gd:214) is its counterpart, so a stored per-category trim is one line in each. No bus, no routing, no new node.

Blocked on geometry, not audio: see -x for the options panel being exactly full. A volume control needs a row and there is no room for one, so decide the way out first (grow the panel, or split audio onto its own screen the way Keys already is).

Note the seam discipline that applies: tune_voice is assertable headless precisely because it takes its target as an argument, so a trim added there stays testable. Adding it inside play() instead would put it back behind should_play and out of reach. See .claude/skills/extract-a-testable-seam.

ACCEPTANCE: music and effects each have a level the player can set and the game remembers; a headless test asserts the trim reaches tune_voice and _start rather than only that the setting is stored.

title: Assert the sound table has no accidental twins, from the table itself
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (73)', first entry -- the gate half, split out per the rule that an acceptance a commit cannot produce is its own item. This one a commit CAN produce, and it is what stops the fix from rotting.

Sfx.SOUNDS (game/sfx.gd:86) and Sfx.VOLUME_DB (:150) are both const Dictionaries, so a test can derive every (file, volume) pair and assert no two ids collide -- without anyone maintaining a list of known pairs. That is derive-the-list applied to a table this project already owns.

One sharing is deliberate and must be waived IN THE CODE rather than in the test: WAVE_CLEARED reusing RUN_WON's jingle at a lower volume is documented at game/sfx.gd:95 and is the pattern to imitate. A waiver list living in the test is a second source of truth; a waiver beside the entry is a comment someone reads while editing it.

Note this test can be written BEFORE -2r8g lands, and should be -- it will fail, naming the four collisions, which is a better specification of that work than the bead description is.

ACCEPTANCE: the check derives pairs from the two dictionaries; a deliberate sharing is expressed at the SOUNDS entry, not in the test; a mutation adding a fifth collision goes red.
close_reason: Both shipped in a12cb8e. The derived check found five collisions where a hand-read had found two; PITCH is a third mixer axis with a stated direction (losses lower, gains higher); Sfx.tune_voice is the seam that makes the table's uniqueness mean something, after a mutation deleting the pitch line survived the table check.

title: Give a loss and a no-op different sounds
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (73)', first entry. PLAYER-FACING. Derived from the full SOUNDS table, not sampled.

Sfx.SOUNDS (game/sfx.gd:86) maps 22 named beats onto 11 distinct .ogg files. Ten sharings, one documented as deliberate (game/sfx.gd:95 -- WAVE_CLEARED reuses RUN_WON at -9.0 against -4.0, so the same phrase reads as the smaller version of the same event, which is right).

Two share a file AND a volume, which makes them the same sound to a player:
  - PEST_ESCAPED and PURCHASE_DENIED, both error_002.ogg at default (game/sfx.gd:91, :106). One costs a life. The other costs nothing.
  - PLANT_DESTROYED and CHOMP_BITE, both chop.ogg at default (:89, :119). Your plant dying sounds like your plant eating.

Two more share a file and differ only in volume: PLANT_BITTEN / CORN_FIRED (impactSoft_medium_002.ogg, -8.0 vs default) and HUSK_ROTTED / BUTTON_PRESSED (minimize_006.ogg, -6.0 vs -10.0).

This is the two-channel rule the drawn cues already obey, applied to audio: a loss and a no-op should not be separable only by context. Start with the two identical pairs -- they are the ones where no amount of attention helps.

The cheapest fix may not be four new files. VOLUME_DB and REPEAT_MS already exist per id; a pitch shift is a third axis the mixer does not currently use at all, and would keep the palette coherent.

ACCEPTANCE: no two ids share a file at the same volume; a test asserts that from the SOUNDS and VOLUME_DB tables rather than from a list someone typed.
close_reason: Both shipped in a12cb8e. The derived check found five collisions where a hand-read had found two; PITCH is a third mixer axis with a stated direction (losses lower, gains higher); Sfx.tune_voice is the seam that makes the table's uniqueness mean something, after a mutation deleting the pitch line survived the table check.

title: Find out whether a pest killed headless ever frees
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (72)', second entry. A measurement, not a claim -- nobody has taken it.

Plant.play_exit_and_free (game/plant.gd:329-332) frees on the spot when animations are gated off, and test_a_plant_eaten_down_to_nothing_still_frees_the_node_headless plus test_uprooting_plays_its_own_cue_and_still_frees_the_node_headless (test/unit/test_placement.gd) exist because that bug shipped twice.

Pest._play_death (game/pest.gd:866-882) takes the other route. It guards is_inside_tree(), then queues tween_interval(DEATH_LINGER) and tween_callback(queue_free) in BOTH branches -- so headless it depends on a Tween interval elapsing rather than on an early return. Nothing asserts it does.

This is the exact failure class the two plant tests were written for, on the object the game creates most. Whether it leaks depends on whether the suite pumps enough frames for a 0.35s interval, which is a fact about the runner nobody has written down either.

ACCEPTANCE: a headless test that kills a pest and asserts the node is gone, or a recorded finding that it is not, with the frame count the runner actually pumps.
close_reason: Measured: a pest killed headless frees in 18 process frames. No leak. The useful finding is that 18 is far more than the 2 frames _pump gives, so a test checking the tree soon after a kill sees a corpse. Pinned in test_a_pest_killed_headless_is_eventually_freed. c44edb4

title: Name the plant flourish timings, which are the only magic numbers left
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (72)', first entry. Enumerated over every tween_property / tween_method / tween_interval in game/ -- 20 steps across 14 files -- so this is a complete census rather than an impression.

Every animation outside the plant family names its duration: PREP_BAR_PULSE_SECONDS 0.24, PANEL_RISE_SECONDS 0.16, READOUT_PUNCH_SECONDS 0.16 (game/hud.gd:171, :431, :445), CROSSFADE_SECONDS, TURN_SECONDS, RISE_SECONDS, FLIGHT_SECONDS, and Pest HIT_FLASH_DURATION 0.10 with DEATH_LINGER 0.35 / DEATH_FADE 0.15 (game/pest.gd:214, :200, :204). Pest even splits its flash 0.35/0.65 OF the named constant rather than writing two numbers.

The five plant flourishes name nothing. game/plant.gd:272-273 and :331, game/corn_cobbler.gd:183-184 and :331-332, game/chomp_flower.gd:155-156, game/dandelion.gd:390-391 -- eleven bare literals between 0.05 and 0.18. They are also the ones a designer would most want to tune together, since every one is the same gesture: a squash and a return.

Not just a rename. The right shape is probably one constant pair on Plant (out, back) that each subclass scales, because the four peaks differ and the timings barely do.

ACCEPTANCE: no bare duration literal survives in a plant tween; a test asserts the out-and-back pair rather than each call site.

title: Use step-time --then-pause, or find out why nobody ever has
description:
SOURCE: log-devtools.md, cycle 71 entry. From the harness reflection, not from kanban.

Cycle 71 needed to read two transforms during a 0.15s tween. The bus round-trip outran it twice -- both reads returned the landed value, which is indistinguishable from a tween that never started -- and the third poll caught it by luck. pause does not help: pausing is a second command and the tween lands during the round-trip, the same race.

step-time --then-pause exists for exactly this and freezes the tree the moment the step lands, so a step-and-read pair carries no ambient drift. This project has run 71 cycles and roughly 1200 verb calls and has never used it once. Either it is the right tool and the loop does not know it, or it does not work for a Tween (which advances on process time, and the question is whether a stepped-then-paused frame has run the tween's interpolation before the freeze).

Also record the smaller thing found the same way: set-game-speed takes its scale POSITIONALLY, not as --scale. Passing --scale exits 2 with the usage block.

ACCEPTANCE: one worked example driven against a real sub-second tween, written into read-a-moving-value if it works and into log-devtools.md as a gap if it does not.
close_reason: Premise corrected (step-time --then-pause HAS been used, log-devtools.md:3378) and the real question answered: it works on Tweens, deterministically, provided you pause BEFORE creating the tween. Recipe in read-a-moving-value. 4b3d1c3

title: Let a plant flinch when something bites it
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (71)', first entry. PLAYER-FACING.

Three continuous idle animations now exist and they are the same shape: Plant._wobble (game/plant.gd:351), Pest._gait (game/pest.gd:733), and TitleScreen's lawn. A sinusoid cannot be interrupted, so nothing on the board ever flinches -- a bed under attack looks exactly like one that is not.

The state to hang it on exists on both sides already. Plant._quiet_time (game/plant.gd:180) is reset by damage and is what gates regrowth. Pest already varies gait_stretch when hungry (game/pest.gd:780).

Shape: a one-off amplitude term decaying back into the sine, on the same _wobble_time clock -- not a Tween, which would fight the pivot the same way an idle scale would have fought _sprite.scale. It goes on _sway_pivot for exactly that reason.

Watch the mutation traps this subsystem has already sprung twice: past animations_enabled() nothing in _wobble runs headless, so the assertable part must be a pure function (see Plant.breathe_scale), and an assertion expressed relative to the flinch amplitude will pass when that amplitude is zero. Put an absolute floor in pixels.

ACCEPTANCE: a bed being eaten is distinguishable from one that is not, without reading its health bar; a pure function carries the flinch curve and a mutation zeroing it goes red.

title: Give one plant idle motion, and see whether the board comes alive
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md, 'Requested directly by James -- not grown, asked for', first bullet. OUTSIDE this cycle's neighbourhood by the workflow's own rule, and it is the user's own standing ask rather than something the loop grew.

The ask: 'idle motion -- sway, breathe, twitch -- on every plant and pest, not just reaction poses for the moments the game already hooks.'

Verified unbuilt, and the entry is accurate. Every create_tween() on a plant is event-driven: game/plant.gd:237 and :296, game/sunflower.gd:173 and :176 (payout pop and flash), game/corn_cobbler.gd:182 (recoil) and :330, game/chomp_flower.gd:154 (bite), game/dandelion.gd:389. Nothing runs while a plant is doing nothing. ChompFlower's _idle_texture (:42) is a SPRITE SWAP for the bite states, not motion.

File it as one plant rather than five: a sway is a taste call, and the cheapest way to make a taste call is to look at one. The Sunflower is the right first subject -- it is the plant a player stares at while waiting, it already owns a gauge that draws every frame, and it has no aim to fight with.

Watch the cost the rest of the codebase already worries about: Sunflower._drawn_fill_height and CornCobbler.READINESS_STEPS both exist to stop a per-frame value queuing a redraw per frame. An idle tween on _sprite.rotation or scale moves the SPRITE, not the _draw() layer, so it should not touch that -- confirm rather than assume.

ACCEPTANCE: one plant sways while idle; the frame cost is measured with  rather than eyeballed; a screenshot or a short recording shows it, and the decision to extend it to the other four is made afterwards on that evidence.
notes: CORRECTION to the ACCEPTANCE line above, which lost a word to a shell backtick when it was filed: the frame cost is measured with the devtools "performance" verb rather than eyeballed. Filing note for the next cycle: never put backticks in a bd description passed through bash -- they are command substitution, and the word simply vanishes with no error.
close_reason: The bead was wrong: Plant._wobble has swayed every plant since the first playable build and Pest._gait animates pests. Cycle 70 filed it 'verified unbuilt' after enumerating create_tween() sites -- the wrong set, since both are _process sinusoids. The real gap was narrower (a plant had one channel, a pest two) and shipped in 4ad45ed.

title: Sweep the Chomp's chew ring instead of shrinking it
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (70)', second entry. PLAYER-FACING.

game/chomp_flower.gd:135 computes CHEW_RING_RADIUS * (1.0 - chew_progress()) and returns early below 0.5 px. So 'the mouth is nearly free' -- the moment a player is deciding whether to commit a lane -- is drawn smallest, faintest and deepest inside the flower's own sprite, which draws on top of it.

game/husk_layer.gd:69-77 faces the identical problem and answers it the other way: the arc holds a fixed radius + RING_GAP around the husk and sweeps its ANGLE down, so a husk about to rot is exactly as visible as a fresh one. Two timers in one game with opposite answers, and the husk's is the better one.

Copying it costs a TAU * frac argument and removes the early return. Note the grammar consequence, which is a bonus: OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md documents the shrinking ring as one of two exceptions to 'solid ring = a reach', and a swept arc is a vocabulary item the game already has (see -c6qs).

ACCEPTANCE: chew progress is legible at 90% complete; a test asserts the drawn radius no longer varies with progress while the swept angle does.

title: Screenshot the two remaining cues that sit inside their own sprite
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (70)', first entry. The evidence half, split out per the workflow rule cycle 70 added -- a criterion a commit cannot produce is its own bead.

game/plant.gd:172 adds _sprite as a CHILD, and a Node2D draws its own _draw() before its children, so every cue a plant paints is under its own art where they overlap. Enumerated against the 64x64 sprite box (all five plant SVGs are width=64 height=64):
  - cob pips, 20-22 px out (game/corn_cobbler.gd:175-176) -- MEASURED occluded at some aims
  - Chomp chew ring, 16 px down to nothing (game/chomp_flower.gd:24) -- unchecked
  - Sunflower gauge, x -30..-24, y 10..30 (game/sunflower.gd:46-49) -- unchecked
  - Sundew sap 118 px (game/sticky_sundew.gd:34), Dandelion ring 176 (game/dandelion.gd:376) -- mostly clear

Whether the two unchecked ones are hidden depends on the art's alpha where they land. That is a screenshot, and nobody has spent the minute.

Note the harness limit found in the same run and filed as gh#49: sample-pixels can describe a region but cannot assert a colour is present in it, so this is a look-at-the-PNG job until that lands.

ACCEPTANCE: a rendered frame per cue, with a verdict; if either is hidden, either fix it (a cue child drawn above the sprite) or write next to _build_visuals why it is fine.

title: 'More waves, and bosses' has drifted on both halves -- re-read it and say what is left
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'Requested directly by James -- not grown, asked for', the second bullet. OUTSIDE this cycle's neighbourhood, per the workflow's own rule, and taken from one of the file's oldest sections.

The entry says: 'The wave table (WaveDirector) currently ends at 8 fixed waves before endless mode takes over with escalating mutation chance on the same two pests. Add real additional waves to the table, and at least one boss pest -- bigger health pool, a distinct sprite, a mechanic that isn't just armoured but more.'

Both factual halves are now false, and the entry still reads as a request nobody has touched:
- The table does NOT end at 8. game/wave_director.gd:164 opens WAVES and the file's own prose discusses wave 16 as a deliberately sized landing point (:90, :155), with endless scales keyed off wave - WAVES.size() (:162).
- There IS a boss mechanic. game/game.gd:796 documents it -- a pest whose species names a split bursts into that many -- WaveDirector.wave_carries_boss() feeds the HUD's prep note (game/game.gd:1757, game/hud.gd:1500).

What is genuinely unbuilt is the narrower half: the boss is the SAME Pest object (game/game.gd:767 says so explicitly), so 'bigger health pool' and 'a distinct sprite' are still missing while 'a mechanic that isn't just armoured but more' shipped.

Run kanban-staleness-audit's bar on it: this is DRIFTED, not STALE and not STILL REAL, and a wrong verdict either way loses something. Rewrite the entry to what is actually true, then decide whether the remaining half is wanted -- a boss with its own body is a different ask from a boss with its own behaviour, and the behaviour is the part that shipped.

ACCEPTANCE: the entry is rewritten with citations for both corrections; the remaining ask is either filed as its own bead or recorded as declined with the reason.

title: Draw the uproot window, which is the one countdown the game hides
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (69)', first entry. PLAYER-FACING.

_uproot_left ticks at game/game.gd:1375 and never leaves game.gd -- outside it the identifier appears only in tests, never in hud.gd. The HUD learns armed-or-not through uproot_armed() (game/game.gd:1340) and never how much is left.

The game already draws exactly this, twice. husk_layer.gd:69-77 sweeps TAU * frac around a husk as its rot timer runs; hud.gd:643-647 drains PrepBar across the top bar over the prep gap. The four-second irreversible decision is the only countdown with nothing on screen.

Cycle 69 guaranteed the prompt the message row the instant it is armed (MESSAGE_DEADLINE). Drawing the remaining fraction under that line is the other half, and the husk arc has already taught the player the shape.

ACCEPTANCE: the armed window is visible without reading the text; a test asserts the drawn fraction tracks _uproot_left rather than merely existing.

title: Put the reach ring on Plant so the grammar is structural
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (68)', first entry.

game/OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md now says a solid plant-sized ring means REACH. Four plants implement that sentence independently: corn_cobbler.gd:148-149, dandelion.gd:376-377, sticky_sundew.gd:456, each with its own fill, edge, alpha and width.

Four implementations of one rule is how a fifth plant means something slightly different by accident -- and the grammar document is advisory, so nothing catches it. A Plant.draw_reach_ring() on the base class makes the rule structural instead.

CAREFUL, and this is the whole difficulty: SelectionMarker's header documents that CornCobbler and ChompFlower fully override Plant._draw() and never call super, which is why selection cues live in a child node. A base-class draw helper has the same trap -- it must be a function the subclass CALLS, not something drawn in Plant._draw() and hoped for.

ACCEPTANCE: one implementation; each plant passes only its own radius and colour; a test asserts every plant with a reach draws a ring at that reach.

title: Write down the drawn-overlay grammar before a fifth cue guesses at it
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (67)', second entry.

Four cues now share a visual grammar: dashed rings are a REMARK (PlacementPreview._draw_risk_ring, SoleCoverMarks' holds-nothing ring), solid rings are a RANGE, filled dots are 'you would gain this', a doubled line width is an ARMED warning.

Each was decided in its own cycle with its own reasoning and they are consistent -- but the consistency is an accident of taste rather than a rule anyone could apply to a fifth cue. art_src/STYLE.md states the art conventions and has no equivalent for the drawn overlays, which is where four cycles of UI work went.

This is cheap now and expensive later: the grammar is still small enough to state in ten lines, and every cue added before it is written is a chance to contradict it by accident. The two-channel rule (colour is never alone) is already project-wide and belongs at the top of it.

ACCEPTANCE: the grammar is written where a person adding a cue will find it, and each existing cue is checked against it.
close_reason: game/OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md written from the 55 draw calls rather than from memory, with the two places the grammar does NOT hold named. Mechanical half pinned by a test, six mutations red. Pointers added to the three cue headers.

title: Warn at startup when a build begins with rows at floor
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (67)', first entry.

cmd budgets now reports '3 of 7 at floor' with the ids, but only to whoever runs the verb -- which is a developer with a bridge attached. A designer nudging a font size or lengthening a plant name gets no signal until a test fails, and that failure names a BUDGET rather than the change that spent it.

Game.check_budgets() already runs at startup and already builds a report. The count is now one field (at_floor / at_floor_ids on the budgets reply, Game.budgets_at_floor as the static). A single push_warning naming the at-floor rows would put it in the editor output where the person spending the room is looking.

Careful about noise: three rows are PERMANENTLY at floor by ratchet, so an unconditional warning every launch is wallpaper within a day. Warn on a CHANGE -- a row that was not at floor last build and is now -- or say nothing.

ACCEPTANCE: a build that newly spends a row's last pixel says so at startup; a build that merely inherits three at-floor rows does not.

title: Report how many budgets are at their floor
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (66)', first entry.

Three of seven budgets sit exactly at their declared floor -- husk_click 4 of 32, hud_readouts 10 of 171, hud_stats_row 19 of 1112, each precisely its BUDGET_FLOOR value (game/game.gd:1887-1899). That is the ratchet working as designed, and it means the HUD has no room on three rows out of four.

Nothing says so. `cmd budgets` prints seven independent readings and a reader has to compare each headroom against each floor by hand -- which is what cycle 66 did, and it is the only reason anyone knows.

One line on the verb turns seven measurements into a state: '3 of 7 at floor'. Cheap, and it is the number that answers 'can I afford a pixel here?' without arithmetic.

Note the neighbour: -rd9s proposes reporting the worst RECURRING string beside the worst possible one. Both are 'the verb has the data and reports the harder-to-use half'. Do them together if either is worth doing.

ACCEPTANCE: the verb reports the at-floor count; a test asserts it against a budget moved off its floor.
close_reason: cmd budgets now ends '3 of 7 at floor (ids)'. Game.budgets_at_floor is a static beside budget_regressions, five mutations red. Reading the live verb caught pest_road_ceiling qualifying by construction, which would have made every reading say 4 with one permanent entry.

title: Mark an escape the way a death is marked
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (65)', third entry. PLAYER-FACING, and the loudest remaining instance of the asymmetry generator.

A killed pest gets a sound, a corpse sprite, a DEATH_LINGER beat on screen and -- since cycle 65 -- a corpse that says what killed it. A pest that reaches the house and costs a garden bed exits INSTANTLY. The single most consequential event in the game is its least marked.

That is exactly the shape that produced the last three shipped ideas: the husk had a sound and the Sunflower did not; everything downstream of the wave button had a voice and the button did not; the Keys screen existed and the Options screen did not. Each was one line and each was invisible until someone named the pair.

Careful about tone: a death is a small win and can be cheerful. An escape is a loss and the marking should not read as celebration -- and it fires at the moment the player is already being told they lost a bed, so it must not stack into noise.

ACCEPTANCE: an escape is as legible as a kill; a test drives one and asserts the cue.
close_reason: ALREADY SHIPPED, and the bead was wrong. An escape plays Sfx.PEST_ESCAPED (game.gd:911), tints the exit cell via _note_lane_loss (game.gd:910), and punches the Garden readout (hud.gd:1072-1073). Only a beat on the pest itself is missing, and the exit bracket sits under the side panel so it would fade unseen. kanban entry corrected in place; workflow gained the rule that a comparison needs a citation for BOTH halves.

title: Audit the second 'of 30' numbering run (sections 25-27 at lines 633-708)
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's audit. There are TWO independent 'N of 30' numbering runs in kanban.md and cycle 64 audited only one of them.

The run just deleted was subtitled 'grown from the features above' (was at lines 2537-2620). The OTHER run is at lines 633-708 and is subtitled differently -- '(27 of 30) a green test proved nothing, and the suite cannot tell', '(26 of 30) what a reverted upgrade exposed about our own tests', '(25 of 30) three screens learned the same lesson separately'.

Those subtitles suggest a much later and more technical batch than the one audited, so expect a different mix: the deleted run was 6 shipped / 2 stale / 0 wanted, and this one may well hold real work.

CUT BY LINE NUMBER, NOT BY HEADING -- the two runs share heading prefixes, which is how cycle 64 nearly deleted 1937 lines. The skill now says so.

ACCEPTANCE: a verdict table with evidence per entry; STILL REAL ones become beads.

title: Audit kanban's oldest sections, still untouched after three filings
description:
SOURCE: step 0's third pre-flight item. DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THIS CYCLE'S NEIGHBOURHOOD -- cycles 62 and 63 were both inside one Python checker.

NOTE: -tkdz covers pruning the Done section and is open at P2 after being identified twice. This is the IDEA BACKLOG rather than Done -- the historical 'New this cycle' sections, which the file's own top says are roughly half stale.

kanban.md is now past 2400 lines and every cycle appends three more entries to the top. The oldest sections predate the file:line rule added in cycle 31, so their claims about the code are unfalsifiable by construction -- which is exactly what makes them rot rather than resolve.

Use kanban-staleness-audit. Its bar: before writing that something is missing, open the code that would contain it. Expect a third shipped, a third stale, a third still real, and the value is in knowing which.

ACCEPTANCE: the six oldest cycle sections are each resolved -- deleted with a commit cited, promoted to a bead, or given the file:line that makes them checkable.
close_reason: Audited the three oldest backlog sections (the 'grown from the features above' run, 25-27 of 30). 8 entries: 6 SHIPPED, 2 STALE, 0 still real -- all three sections deleted, verdict table in the commit. Near-miss caught before commit: the headings are not unique.

title: Decide whether the other HUD surfaces deserve corpus-style checking
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (63)', first entry. A JUDGEMENT to make once, not a checker to write reflexively.

The message row now has three checkers because it broke three times. The stats row has WORST_CASE_TEXT plus two assertions (-rq94 open), the selection panel has comments and one hand measurement (-r722 open), the run summary has a clearance gate and nothing about content.

The honest question is whether 'has not broken yet' is evidence of safety or of nobody looking. Cycle 45 set the precedent for answering this properly: it decided NOT to build a checker after measuring that precision would be low (9 candidates, 1 real) and recorded the measurement. Do the same here rather than defaulting either way.

Cheap version first: for each of the three surfaces, ask what would have to change for a string to clip, and whether anything would notice. Write the answer down. Only build where the answer is 'nothing would notice'.

ACCEPTANCE: a written verdict per surface with its reasoning; any checker built cites the verdict that justified it.

title: Ask whether the message queue may defer an important message at all
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (63)', third entry. PLAYER-FACING, and it is a design question before it is a code change.

Every check on the message row is about ONE string at ONE instant -- width, corpus membership, variant pricing. _message_queue (game/hud.gd) holds several, each with its own lifetime, and the player's experience is the SEQUENCE.

Cycle 61 hit this from the test side: a second armed-uproot prompt read stale because the first was still on screen, and the row had to be drained before the assertion could see anything. That is the same mechanism a player meets when a four-second irreversible prompt lands behind two ambient husk messages.

MESSAGE_IMPORTANT already exists and controls queue priority, so the machinery is there. The question this bead asks is sharper than -xvub's styling one: should an important message be able to WAIT at all, or should it pre-empt? A prompt with a live four-second trigger behind it is not the same kind of object as 'Composted a husk for 3 seeds'.

Measure before deciding: drive a wave, count how often an IMPORTANT message is queued behind an ambient one and for how long. If the answer is 'never in practice', say so and close it -- that is a real result.

ACCEPTANCE: a measured answer, then a decision recorded either way.
close_reason: Measured, then decided. Never behind an ambient line (hud.gd:1429 pre-empts); up to 3.8s behind another important one, against a 4.0s window. Added MESSAGE_DEADLINE and moved the armed-uproot prompt to it. b776202

title: Find message producers nothing calls
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (62)', first entry.

message_corpus_check now verifies every show_message() call site resolves to the corpus, and that a producer with N bool modes appears 2^N times. Neither rule covers the opposite direction: a producer that exists in hud.gd, sits in the corpus, and is called by NOTHING.

Dead message text still being priced sets the row's budget from a string the game can no longer produce -- the same lie as an unpriced string with the sign flipped, and it is the direction derive-the-list warns about (a recorded list with a one-directional test).

The set is enumerable now, which is what makes this cheap: the corpus names the producers, and a scan of game/*.gd says which are called. suite_reach_check does the same shape for functions no TEST names; this is functions no CALLER names.

Careful about the waived call sites: a producer reached only through a waived, runtime-assembled path would look uncalled. Check against the waiver list before reporting.

ACCEPTANCE: a corpus producer with no call site is a finding; fixture proves it fires and that a waived caller does not trip it.
close_reason: Third rule added: a corpus producer nothing calls. Clean on this repo (all 7 have callers), so the fixture is its whole evidence -- 4 cases including 'only the HUD itself calls it', 4 mutations all red. Writing it caught the rule ignoring its own advertised waiver. 1bee643

title: Check the notebook still reads right with a non-TABLE id in the save
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's implementation review.

HINT_MOVE_PREVIEW is stored in earned_milestones, which is the achievement set. Cycle 61 verified by READING that the notebook is immune -- its shelf rows and its 'N of M earned' count both iterate Milestones.TABLE (notebook_screen.gd:487), and that function's own header says this is deliberate so a foreign id cannot inflate the total.

That verification was static. Nothing DRIVES the notebook with a foreign id present, so the protection is a comment plus a reading rather than a test -- and it is now load-bearing for a feature that ships.

Cheap to close: instantiate the notebook with HINT_MOVE_PREVIEW recorded and assert the shelf count and row set are unchanged. That also pins the claim for whoever adds the second hint (-above).

ACCEPTANCE: a test drives the notebook with a non-TABLE id recorded and asserts nothing moved.

title: Point a second one-shot hint at something else nobody finds
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (61)', first entry. PLAYER-FACING.

The one-shot mechanism now exists (RunConfig.HINT_MOVE_PREVIEW) and costs one constant and one bool. It teaches exactly one thing.

Candidates, all currently discovered by accident or not at all: the husk sweep, the uproot refund, the packet tiers, the colourblind toggle.

The restraint worth keeping: a hint should point at something the player can act on IN THAT MOMENT, which is why the move tip lives on the armed prompt rather than in a tutorial. A hint fired at a moment the player cannot use it is worse than none, because it spends the row AND the attention.

Pick ONE. Four hints firing in a first session is a tutorial nobody asked for, and the message row is at 86% of capacity (-r722, and the recurring-case bead above).

ACCEPTANCE: one new hint, fired at a moment it is actionable, with its worst-case string in the corpus.

title: Price a producer's boolean variants, not just its call sites
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (61)', third entry.

Hud.uproot_armed_message now takes a `with_tip` bool, and message_corpus() has to append BOTH forms by hand. Cycle 61's corpus test caught the omission only because it counts entries per plant and the number moved from 3 to 4 -- an accident of arithmetic, not a check of the thing.

tools/message_corpus_check.py verifies every show_message CALL SITE resolves to the corpus. It does not verify that every VARIANT of a producer is in it. A producer with N boolean modes has 2^N strings and only the ones someone typed get priced -- so the row's budget silently prices a subset again, which is the exact defect the corpus was built in cycle 52 to end.

Detectable statically: a producer whose signature has bool parameters, appearing in message_corpus() fewer than 2^N times, is a finding. Two producers, one variant each, is the whole current corpus -- so the fixture matters more than the corpus here.

ACCEPTANCE: adding a bool to a message producer without adding its variant to the corpus is a finding; fixture proves it fires.
close_reason: message_corpus_check now prices a producer's bool VARIANTS, not just its call sites. Found next_wave_note (2 bools, 1 of 4 priced) on its first run; waived after checking both flags only append. 7 fixture cases, 5 mutations all red.

title: Re-capture the UI findings baseline, which no longer exists
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's step 4.

`findings` reported '4 NEW, 0 pre-existing' this cycle. The standing note in cycle-log says the UI baseline carries twelve overlaps acceptable only while both controls are unreachable -- so a baseline WAS captured once and this run saw none.

Likely cause: it lives in user:// and this session has been relaunching with `--snapshot-userstate 'highscore.save'`, which restores only that one file. Whatever the cause, the effect is that every ui_layout finding now gates as NEW, including transient ones -- this cycle's four were the selection panel caught mid-entrance-fade by a pause.

Verify the twelve overlaps are still the right set BEFORE re-banking (they are only acceptable while both controls are unreachable, and two new drawn cues have shipped since). Do not save-ui-baseline blindly -- that is exactly the 'improvement buries a regression' trap house-static-checker now warns about.

ACCEPTANCE: a baseline exists again, and its contents were checked rather than banked.

title: Make an important message look important
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (60)', third entry. PLAYER-FACING.

MESSAGE_IMPORTANT (game/hud.gd:336) controls queue PRIORITY, not appearance. So the armed-uproot prompt -- which carries a four-second irreversible decision -- looks exactly like 'Composted a husk for 3 seeds.'

A player learns to skim that row because most of what it says is ambient. The one line that must be read is styled identically to the ones that need not be.

Two-channel rule applies: it cannot be colour alone. A weight change, a small icon, or a brief hold before the queue advances would each carry it. The hold is interesting because it costs no pixels on a row that is already tight (see -r722 and the one-shot bead).

ACCEPTANCE: important and ambient messages are distinguishable with colour thrown away; a test asserts the distinction on both kinds.

title: Sweep tools/ for other guards no mutation can kill
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's step 4. A mutation SURVIVED and that was the finding.

_update_preview guarded on `_uproot_armed if _uproot_left > 0.0`, and the second half was unkillable: _disarm_uproot() nulls the first on every exit path. Dead code wearing a safety belt, which this repo has paid for once already in mirror_check's CRLF normalisation -- found the same way, by mutating and watching nothing go red.

Two instances is a pattern. The candidates are compound conditions where both halves are maintained by the same writer: `x != null and x_count > 0`, `armed and time_left > 0`, `visible and not empty`. Grep for `and` in guards, and for each ask: can these two ever disagree?

Do NOT delete on suspicion -- a guard that cannot disagree TODAY may be the thing stopping them diverging tomorrow. The test is whether an invariant elsewhere guarantees it, and if so that invariant deserves the test instead.

ACCEPTANCE: a per-candidate verdict; anything removed leaves its invariant as a test.

title: Decide whether moving a plant should cost anything
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (59)', second entry. BALANCE DECISION, needs a call before it needs code.

The window now arms, previews, and then either destroys or cancels. The player still has to uproot, re-select from the shop and pay full price -- so the move preview shows them a decision the game then charges them full price to act on.

Every piece for 'click the destination to move it there' exists: arm_uproot knows the plant, the preview knows the destination, uproot_refund() knows the rebate.

The open question is price, and it is a real balance question rather than an oversight: free moves make placement mistakes costless and remove a whole layer of decision; full price makes the preview cruel; the refund-minus-cost difference is the middle and is already computed. Pick deliberately.

Depends on -eupm (showing the net cost), which is the same arithmetic surfaced.

ACCEPTANCE: a decision recorded with its reasoning, then the implementation.

title: Preview the destination while an uproot is armed
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (58)', first entry. PLAYER-FACING, and the natural completion of three cycles of work.

Arming an uproot reddens the rings on the cells that go bare (cycle 58). PlacementPreview's dots already say what a plant would newly defend at a hovered cell (cycle 55). While an uproot is armed the game knows BOTH the plant's kind and that a move is being weighed, so hovering a destination in that window could show the dots for THIS plant at THAT cell.

That turns two separate reads into a move preview, which is what the player is actually doing. No new computation: _preview.reach and _preview.covered_now already take whatever they are given.

Careful: the armed window is four seconds (Game.UPROOT_CONFIRM_SECONDS) and the preview is normally driven by the SELECTED shop plant, so this must not leave the preview stuck showing the uprooted plant's reach after the window lapses. Test the lapse, not just the arm -- cycle 46 nearly filed a defect against a correctly-lapsed uproot window.

ACCEPTANCE: hovering while armed previews the selected plant's reach at the hover cell; letting the window lapse restores the normal preview; a test drives all three states.
close_reason: While an uproot is armed the hover previews the plant being MOVED, with that plant excluded from covered_now. Red rings (what it costs) and green dots (what it buys) are on screen together. Removed a guard no mutation could kill and replaced it with the invariant as a test. Unified sole_cover_cells onto covered_road_cells(except).

title: Preview the move when an uproot is armed
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (57)', third entry. PLAYER-FACING.

Arming an uproot (Game.arm_uproot) is the exact moment the game knows a MOVE is being considered, and it currently changes only the button's text to 'Really uproot? (+N)'.

Everything needed to show the consequence already exists: sole_cover_cells says what the road loses, and PlacementPreview's dots say what a replacement would newly defend. Arming could put the plant's sole-cover rings into a warning state -- these are the cells that go bare if you confirm -- which is the same data with the tense changed.

This is the strongest of the three uproot-adjacent ideas because it needs no new computation and no new node, only a state on SoleCoverMarks. SelectionMarker already has a WARNING_COLOR and set_warning() for exactly this kind of escalation.

ACCEPTANCE: arming an uproot restyles the rings; committing or letting the window lapse restores them; a test drives all three states.
close_reason: Arming an uproot now reddens the sole-cover rings, in the same red and with the same doubling as the brackets. Deliberately NOT the holds-nothing ring: no cells are lost there, so warning would be a false alarm about the one free uproot. Five mutations kill it. efe2c4f..HEAD

title: Budget the selection panel, which is full and priced only in comments
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (57)', first entry.

Every constraint on the selection panel is prose or a hand measurement: _selection_label autowraps with a 56px minimum (game/hud.gd:720) inside a 152px SelectionBox; the VBox comment (game/hud.gd:1203) says the stack runs to within 16px of the panel foot; hud.gd's own header records that a third line once pushed the foot to exactly 648 and was caught by the clearance gate.

Cycle 57 measured the cob's second line at ~190px of a 232px box BY HAND to decide against adding text there. That measurement is now lost.

Game.budget_entries() (game/game.gd:1921) prices five couplings and this is not one of them, though it is the same shape as hud_message_row exactly: a fixed box, a worst-case string set, and a failure mode (wrap -> push the buttons out) that no per-Control check sees. Reuse Hud.message_corpus()'s pattern -- declare the worst case for each plant type's two lines beside the code that builds them.

ACCEPTANCE: a hud_selection_panel budget with a floor; it reports the widest per-plant line and the remaining vertical room; a deliberately worsened line trips it.

title: Check the two new cues against the colourblind ramp
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's implementation review.

SoleCoverMarks uses SelectionMarker.MARKER_COLOR (yellow) and PlacementPreview's dots use its own green marker_color. Neither was checked against the colourblind-safe ramp, and this project has a standing two-channel rule: colour is never the only signal.

The two cues DO differ in shape (filled disc versus outline ring) and in when they appear, so the rule is probably satisfied -- but 'probably' is exactly the word that made the road overlay's header spell its own channel argument out in full. Game.repaint_for_palette() exists and neither new node is wired into it.

ACCEPTANCE: a written verdict per cue; either wired into repaint_for_palette or a comment saying why shape alone carries it.

title: Name the coverage-is-not-engagement mechanic on the run summary
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (56)', third entry. PLAYER-FACING.

Three cycles have measured it: a cob fires at the furthest-along pest only, so five cobs covering all 32 road cells lose a pest that seven covering the SAME cells stop. The player currently learns this by losing, if at all.

game/run_summary.gd already reports beds lost and pests that walked in untouched, so the surface and the data both exist. A line comparing road covered against pests nothing shot at names the mechanic in the one place a player reads carefully.

Overlaps -dgu5 (a reach-par on the same screen) -- do them together or the summary grows two lines about the same idea. This one is the more important half: a par without the mechanic behind it reads as 'you used too many plants', which is the opposite of true.

ACCEPTANCE: the summary states the distinction in the player's own terms; a test asserts the line against a run with known coverage and known untouched pests.

title: Screenshot a hover and a selection at once, and see if the cues collide
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (56)', second entry.

The hover dots (filled 4 px green discs, PlacementPreview) and the selection rings (9 px yellow outlines, SoleCoverMarks) were deliberately given different shapes so they can share a screen. Nobody has looked at that state.

Both can land on the SAME cell: hovering a new plant whose reach overlaps the selected plant's sole-cover cells is an ordinary thing to do while deciding where to build. A 4 px disc centred inside a 9 px ring may read as one compound mark rather than two facts.

Use godot-hud-occlusion-audit. This is a five-minute job with a screenshot and it is the kind of thing that is invisible in every structural check -- both cues pass their own tests independently.

ACCEPTANCE: a screenshot of the overlapping state and a written verdict; if they collide, one of the two shapes moves.

title: Say 'nothing depends on this one' when a selected plant rings nothing
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (56)', first entry. PLAYER-FACING.

SoleCoverMarks (game/sole_cover_marks.gd) rings the road only the selected plant holds. An empty set now means something concrete and useful: this plant can be uprooted and replanted elsewhere at no cost in coverage.

But an empty set renders as nothing, which is indistinguishable from 'you have not selected anything' or 'the cue is broken' -- and cycle 55 already proved that an absent render is the hardest state to read correctly, since I spent ten minutes on exactly that confusion with the hover dots.

One line in the selection panel turns a silent absence into the advice it already is. Game.arm_uproot is right there, so the sentence can point at the action.

Careful: it must not read as 'uproot this', which is a recommendation the game has no business making -- depth is often exactly what was wanted. 'Nothing depends on this one' states the fact and leaves the decision alone.

ACCEPTANCE: the panel distinguishes 'no rings because nothing is selected' from 'no rings because nothing depends on it'; a test asserts both readings.
close_reason: Solved in the world rather than the panel: an empty sole-cover set now draws a dashed ring around the plant, so 'nothing depends on this' never looks like 'the cue is broken'. The panel had no room -- measured, the cob's second line is ~190px of 232 and the label autowraps. efe2c4f

title: Make the preview cue survive a plant being uprooted mid-hover
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's implementation review.

Game._update_preview recomputes covered_road_cells() on every hover, so the dots are fresh while the mouse moves. But covered_now is only pushed from _update_preview -- if the set changes while the cursor is STILL (a plant is destroyed by a pest, an uproot commits, a wave ends), the dots keep showing the old answer until the mouse moves.

That is the one error this cue must not make, since it is read as 'spend seeds here': marking ground as bare that a plant now covers, or failing to mark ground that just became bare when a plant was eaten.

Cheapest fix: push covered_now from Game._refresh() as well, which already fires on placement, uproot and destruction. Verify with the harness rather than by reasoning -- kill a plant while the preview is visible and re-read the dots (see .claude/skills/read-a-moving-value: freeze first).

ACCEPTANCE: a test that shows the dots updating when a covering plant is destroyed without the hover moving.
close_reason: Fixed in the same cycle it was found. Game._refresh now pushes covered_now and repaints while the preview is visible. Proved live: 8 dots -> 2 when a second cob lands, cursor unmoved.

title: Show what a SELECTED plant uniquely contributes
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (55)', first and third entries. PLAYER-FACING.

The hover cue now answers 'what would this purchase add' (new_cover_cells). Nothing answers the mirror question about a plant already standing: selecting a cob draws its range ring identically whether it is the only thing covering that road or one of three.

That is the question behind 'can I sell this one and move it?', and it is also the depth read the original bead (-ivoq) wanted, asked at the moment it is actionable rather than painted permanently on the road -- which is what -ivoq could not do, because lane_pressure_overlay.gd documents that the road's channels are spent.

The data is the same set difference in the other direction: the cells this plant covers that NO other standing plant covers. Reuse new_cover_cells' shape.

ACCEPTANCE: selecting a plant marks the road only it holds; a test asserts the marks vanish when a second plant covering the same cells is placed.
close_reason: Shipped as SoleCoverMarks: rings on the road cells a selected plant alone covers, pushed from _refresh so they thin when the garden changes without re-selecting. Proved live 8 -> 0 when a second cob lands. New node rather than SelectionMarker because play_entrance tweens that node's scale. 1d4c162

title: Rename shows_redundant_coverage to say it is about patches
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (55)', second entry.

shows_redundant_coverage() (game/placement_preview.gd:349) reads as a general redundancy cue and is specifically about Sundew patch stacking -- it calls StickySundew.added_crossing_time_multiplier and fires only when a second patch multiplies crossing time by 1.0.

For a Corn Cobbler the same word means the OPPOSITE thing: a second cob over identical cells is worth real money, measured in cycle 54 as the difference between a five-cob garden that loses a pest and a seven-cob garden that does not. A reader reaching for 'the redundancy cue' to apply to cobs would find this function and be wrong.

This is scope-vs-claim shape 5 (a NAME claiming more than its body) on a function rather than a test. shows_redundant_patch_coverage() costs a rename and removes the trap. Check covering_patch_count() and previewing_non_stacking_patch() at the same time -- those two already say 'patch' and are the reason the trap is only in the one name.

ACCEPTANCE: the name says patch; the header states plainly that cob stacking is valuable and cites the cycle-54 measurement.

title: Draw coverage DEPTH, not just coverage
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (54)', first entry. PLAYER-FACING.

A cell covered by one cob and a cell covered by three look identical on the board, and _furthest_along_in_range (game/corn_cobbler.gd:109) makes that difference decisive: one cob covering eight cells is busy with exactly one of them.

Cycle 54 proved the gap numerically rather than by argument. Five cobs cover the whole road and let a pest through unfought; seven cover the same road and do not. Same coverage map, different outcome.

The data is one line different from what the board already computes: count the plants whose reach contains the cell instead of asking whether any does. A second, denser tint at depth >= 2 shows the player the thing the coverage map structurally cannot.

Overlaps -a6rf (covered-but-contested), which is the same problem measured at RUNTIME rather than statically. Do this one first: it is static, cheap, and always true, whereas contested-ness flickers.

ACCEPTANCE: depth >= 2 is visually distinct from depth 1; a test asserts the tint over a known garden.
close_reason: Shipped as new-cover dots at hover time rather than a road tint. The bead's design was wrong twice: the road overlay documents that its channels are spent, and 'redundant' is false for cobs (cycle 54 measured seven cobs beating five over identical coverage). new_cover_cells() + _draw_new_cover_dots(), three mutations kill it, confirmed on screen. 701e24f

title: Assert the road invariants explicitly instead of implying them
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's step 5 (workflow reflection).

test_the_road_is_still_the_road_the_constants_were_measured_against asserts 32 cells and the route length, and its failure message names what to re-derive. That is what made this cycle's reshape safe -- but the assertion reads as 'the road has not changed' when what it actually protects is 'the road's LENGTH and CELL COUNT have not changed'.

Those are different claims and the difference is exactly what made the reshape cheap: the shape changed completely and that test correctly stayed silent. A reader who trusts its name would conclude the road is untouched.

This is scope-vs-claim shape 1 on a test name. Rename it and say in the header which properties are guarded and which -- dead ground, garden coverage, the split cell -- are guarded elsewhere and WILL move.

ACCEPTANCE: the name and header state length-and-count rather than identity, and point at the shape-dependent tests by name.

title: Make PATH_CORNERS per-level and derive the shape figures at test time
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (53)', first entry. This is the real unlock behind -84x0 and is worth more than the climb was.

Reshaping the road (game/board.gd:50) cost five test re-derivations this cycle: two dead-ground counts, two garden placement lists, and a split cell. Every one of them is a RECORDED measurement of one specific road.

The invariant trick is the reusable half: hold 32 cells and 2112 px and nothing reasoned from length or cell count moves at all -- SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING's '3.5 pests per cell' survived untouched. What did move is everything shape-dependent.

If the garden lists were DERIVED at test time (greedy set cover at the plant's reach, which is exactly how they were re-derived by hand this cycle) and the dead-ground counts asserted as relations rather than absolutes ('the shorter reach strands strictly more' already is one), a second road becomes a data change.

See .claude/skills/derive-the-list: this is its 'record the list, or derive it at check time?' question, and the answer just changed because the derivation is now written down and cheap.

ACCEPTANCE: a second PATH_CORNERS can be added and the suite passes without editing a recorded number; the invariants that must hold are asserted explicitly.
close_reason: Delivered the derivable half and documented why the rest should NOT be derived. Derived: the walled mouth list and the buildable count. Recorded but now GUARDED by test_the_recorded_gardens_still_have_the_property_they_claim: the two cob gardens, because they encode firepower rather than coverage and derive-the-list calls that a taste call -- deriving them produced a better cover and broke two behavioural tests. dead_corn/dead_chomp left recorded on purpose so a human sees playability move. A second road is now a data change plus two numbers. a00ada2

title: Give tools/ a shared source blanker instead of five copies
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's work on message_corpus_check.py.

That checker needed strip_comments() -- blank # comments and string BODIES, preserving offsets. So do world_control_check, meta_key_check, group_leak_check and settle_read_check. That is five implementations of one transform, and the repo has already been bitten by a subtly wrong one: an escape-blind blanker read '...entry[\\"key\\"]' as live code, found only by mutating the checker.

This cycle added a SIXTH failure mode to the pile: the new checker needed the blanked text for code and the RAW text for string literals, at the same offsets. That dual-reading is subtle enough to deserve one documented home.

A tools/gdsource.py with strip_comments(), first_arg_span() and normalise_literal(), each with the unit test house-static-checker asks for (known-in, known-out on a handful of controlled inputs -- NOT a statistic over the real corpus, which is the guard that cannot fail). Then the five checkers import it.

Careful: they must stay stdlib-only and parallel-safe, so the shared module lives in tools/ and imports nothing.

ACCEPTANCE: one implementation, unit-tested; the five checkers use it; all still exit 0.

title: Tie WORST_CASE_TEXT to the text the readouts are actually assigned
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (52)', first entry.

The message row is solved: Hud.message_corpus() (game/hud.gd:1659) declares the set and tools/message_corpus_check.py ties every show_message() call site to it. The STATS row is one row up and still has the old shape.

WORST_CASE_TEXT (game/hud.gd:76) is a hand-typed table of worst-case strings. Cycle 51 added assertions that the SET of readouts matches the Labels in the row, both directions. Nothing checks that the declared string is actually the widest thing that readout is ever ASSIGNED. _wave_label.text is built at game/hud.gd:1049-1058 from three separate branches (finite wave, endless wave, plus a threat suffix); the declared worst case is one string someone wrote out.

Same defect class as the message row, one row higher, and much cheaper now that the pattern exists: a checker that finds every `_<name>_label.text =` assignment and verifies its format shape is represented in WORST_CASE_TEXT, reusing message_corpus_check's literal normalisation (it already matches '%d' against '99999').

ACCEPTANCE: an assignment whose shape is not declared is a finding; fixture proves it fires; the existing entries are confirmed or corrected.

title: Name show_message's producers in one place beside _paint_message_row
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (51)', second entry.

show_message() has eight call sites: game/game.gd:231 (purchase refusal), :1464 and :1468 (mute), :1605 (placement refusal), plus the four Hud.*_message producers. Nothing names the set, so _budget_hud_message_row had to enumerate it by grepping -- and got it wrong twice, in consecutive cycles, each time adding only the producer that happened to be in view.

Even a comment block beside _paint_message_row listing the producers would make the budget's corpus checkable instead of archaeological. Better still: a static function returning the enumerable worst-case strings, which the budget calls instead of rebuilding the list -- then there is one list and it is the one that is used.

ACCEPTANCE: the budget stops constructing its own corpus; a producer added without joining the set is caught.
close_reason: Hud.message_corpus() declares the set beside its producers; the budget reads it; tools/message_corpus_check.py enforces that every show_message() call site resolves to it or carries a reasoned waiver. 5 waived, 0 findings. a648006

title: Collapse the top bar's three hand-lists of readouts into one table
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (51)', first entry.

The four top-bar readouts are described in THREE places: Hud.WORST_CASE_TEXT (game/hud.gd:76), the four width constants Hud.stats_row_budget() sums (game/hud.gd:944), and the four _add_stat() calls in _build (game/hud.gd:598-601). Until cycle 51 nothing compared any pair, and both gaps that opened were real: a readout could be added to the row and be invisible to WORST_CASE_TEXT, or declared there and invisible to the width sum.

Both are closed by assertions now, so this is not urgent -- but the structure is still three lists and the assertions are scaffolding around it. One table of {name, worst_case_text, width} that _build, the budget and the tests all read removes the class rather than the two instances.

derive-the-list explicitly permits a recorded list plus an equality assertion. It does not permit three of them.

ACCEPTANCE: one declaration; _build, stats_row_budget and the budget all read it; the two cycle-51 assertions become redundant and are deleted rather than left as decoration.

title: Prune the Done section of kanban.md, which nothing has ever read back
description:
SOURCE: step 0's third pre-flight item. DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THIS CYCLE'S NEIGHBOURHOOD -- cycles 49 and 50 were checkers, skills and one pest test.

kanban.md is 2200+ lines and its 'Done' section runs from line 12 to line 167. The file says at its own top that the historical sections are unpruned and roughly half stale, and step 0 tells every cycle to mine the backlog -- but nothing has ever been retired from Done, which is 155 lines of scroll between the reader and the ideas.

Run kanban-staleness-audit over it. Anything genuinely shipped and asserted can go, with the commit that did it noted; anything that says 'done' but has no test is not done and belongs back in the backlog -- that distinction is the actual value here, and it is why this is not just tidying.

ACCEPTANCE: Done is shorter, and every entry removed is either cited to a commit or moved back to the backlog with a reason.
notes: Cycle 64 changes what to expect: the three oldest BACKLOG sections came out 6 shipped / 2 stale / 0 still wanted. Apply the same evidence bar to Done -- an entry needs the file:line AND the gate that holds it, or it moves back to the backlog. 'Done' with no test behind it is not done, and that distinction is the real value in pruning it.

title: Give tools/mutate.py the three-way exit verdict, not just three-way application
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's step 4, extending -ghv1 which was filed last cycle.

-ghv1 asks for a shared mutate.py that distinguishes 'did not apply' from 'survived'. This cycle produced the second half of the same lesson within the hour, in a different costume: a sweep that mutated GAME code against the test suite read all three mutations as killed, because run_tests.py takes --filter only after `--` and argparse exited 2 every time. `if returncode:` is true for 2, and 2 means nothing was verified.

So mutate.py needs BOTH: needle-matched-exactly-once on the way in, and a three-way verdict on the way out (0 SURVIVED / 1 RED / 2 BROKEN RUN), with the run's own denominator printed beside each result. It should also run the restore and FAIL LOUDLY if the unmutated run is not clean -- that is what caught this, and it caught it by accident rather than by design.

Depends on -ghv1; merge into it if that is easier than sequencing.

title: Make the mutation harness distinguish 'did not apply' from 'survived'
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's step 4, the note appended to the log-devtools entry.

Two of four mutations in the first sweep printed MUTATION TEXT NOT FOUND because a shell heredoc ate a backslash level. That reads exactly like 'the code is not present' and a sweep that only checked exit codes would have recorded them as SURVIVED -- i.e. as evidence that two guards were not load-bearing, when in fact they had never been touched. Mine caught it only because I happened to assert the needle was found.

The house-static-checker skill mandates mutating the checker but says nothing about how to run the mutations. Since every checker here now wants this, it is worth a small shared tools/mutate.py: take a file, a list of (label, needle, transform), assert each needle matches EXACTLY ONCE, run a command, and report RED/SURVIVED/NOT-APPLIED as three distinct outcomes. Normalise line endings before matching -- this repo is CRLF and that is a second way a needle silently misses.

ACCEPTANCE: tools/mutate.py exists, reports the three outcomes distinctly, and mirror_check.py's six mutations are expressed with it.

title: Audit the other house checkers for marker-scoped truncation
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's step 4 (harness reflection) and kanban.md 'New this cycle (49)', second entry.

mirror_check.py scoped its comparison between a START heading and an ENDS marker, and ENDS contained '
---
' -- ordinary markdown. A horizontal rule inside the block ended it early in BOTH files, so two 21-character stubs compared identical and the tool reported clean. Fixed in 0c5cb1b by truncation_warning().

Every checker that scopes by a text marker has this failure available to it. Read the scoping in world_control_check.py, meta_key_check.py, group_leak_check.py, svg_style_check.py, suite_reach_check.py, settle_read_check.py and save_persist_check.py, and ask of each: can the region it measures be silently smaller than intended, and would that read as clean?

The guard is cheap and is the SAME denominator rule house-static-checker already states for finding counts, applied to the input instead of the output: assert the region you measured is as big as you expect.

ACCEPTANCE: a per-checker verdict; any checker that can silently measure a stub gains a guard and a fixture case proving it fires.
close_reason: Audited all seven. Files: every denominator matches the real 52-file set. Regions: six immune by construction (func-to-next-func, suffix-to-end, indentation-delimited, depth-tracked with the -1 guarded at meta_key_check.py:399). One weak spot fixed: suite_reach_check.autoload_names() returned {} silently; now reports the count. b563cbb

title: Look at pest facing on screen before working or closing the James request
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md, 'New this cycle (49)', first entry. DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THIS CYCLE'S NEIGHBOURHOOD -- cycle 49 was entirely static tooling and markdown; this needs a running game and a screenshot.

'Fix enemy facing direction' sits under 'Requested directly by James' in kanban.md. The code appears to already do it: Pest._update_facing (game/pest.gd:679) picks all four cardinals from the direction of travel, _apply_facing (game/pest.gd:696) is the single writer of _sprite.rotation and composes facing with the gait sway, and test/unit/test_selftest.gd:8378 asserts that composition.

DO NOT close it on that evidence. The request was made about what the SCREEN looked like, and code implementing a thing is not evidence the screen shows it. The likely remaining defect is downstream: a species whose sprite art does not actually rest up-screen (-Y), which game/pest.gd:675 names as the convention. That is a small art fix, not a feature.

Launch, walk a pest down each of the four road directions, screenshot each, and compare against the convention. See .claude/skills/read-a-moving-value before concluding from any single frame.

ACCEPTANCE: four screenshots or a written per-direction verdict, and the kanban entry either closed with evidence or narrowed to the specific species that is wrong.
close_reason: Already shipped and verified on screen: all four cardinals correct live, all three pest SVGs rest head-up-screen per STYLE.md:14, screenshot confirms. Added the missing assertion (Vector2.UP was in no test; the route never goes -Y). 155beb4

title: Write the pause-before-you-read rule into the devtools skill, not just the gap log
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's step 4 (harness reflection), gap [G-056].

Reading MessageLabel.text returned empty three times while _idle_message held the correct value -- correct behaviour (a transient message outranks the standing note), but a single read of a value a _process timer mutates carries no evidence that it was moving. pause + drain made it deterministic in one try.

G-056 is filed upstream-eligible against the harness docs. The in-project half: this is the THIRD time this session a state variable told the truth a screen read did not (cycle 38's faded banner, cycle 46's lapsed uproot window, this). Three is not a coincidence, it is a missing skill. Candidate: .claude/skills/read-a-moving-value/ -- freeze first, name the variable that holds the truth, and never file a defect from a single live read.

ACCEPTANCE: the skill exists and names all three incidents as its evidence.
close_reason: Built .claude/skills/read-a-moving-value/SKILL.md after the third near-miss this session. 1f20279

title: Check every budget's evidence string against what it actually sweeps
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md, 'New this cycle (48)', second entry.

_budget_hud_message_row (game/game.gd:2037) measured four plant-name messages and not the prep note sharing the row -- wrong by 36px for seven cycles while reporting green, because a budget over a subset always reports MORE headroom than exists. Game.budget_entries (game/game.gd:1852) builds six others the same way, and each names its corpus in a free-text 'evidence' string that nothing checks against the code.

Do the cheap version first: read all seven and ask, for each, 'what else can reach this measurement?' Record the answer per budget. title: Every Sundew redraw walks every pest on the board
description: StickySundew._draw_wash calls shared_ground_offsets, which calls _sibling_patches, which walks all of _entities' children -- and pests live there too. So the cost of drawing one patch scales with the number of pests, not the number of patches. _refresh_droplets queues a redraw whenever droplet_radius changes, which it does as pests enter and leave the patch, so the redraws are most frequent exactly when the pest count is highest. Sundew membership changes at only two sites, so the sibling list could be cached and invalidated there instead.
