title: Audit the notebook against three cycles of new mechanics
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md older sections, via step 6's outside-the-neighbourhood rule. The notebook is the one player-facing surface untouched in the last seven cycles, and it is the surface whose whole job is to describe the game to the player.

Cycles 69-75 added or changed: a third message priority rung with an armed-uproot prompt that now pre-empts (MESSAGE_DEADLINE), a spread arc whose presence marks a Corn Cobbler level, an idle breathe on every plant, a corpse whose shape names its cause, and a pitch axis on the sound palette where losses go lower.

The question is not whether the notebook is wrong -- it is whether it still claims to be complete. Its shelf and its drawing pages were written when the game was smaller, and kanban-staleness-audit bar applies to a screen exactly as it does to a backlog entry: open the code that would contain the claim before writing that it is missing.

Verify before claiming anything, and say in the finding HOW. Two of my last four absence claims about this codebase were wrong, both because the enumeration was over the wrong set.

ACCEPTANCE: a verdict per notebook page -- accurate, drifted, or silent about something the player now meets -- with a file:line for each; anything worth adding becomes its own bead rather than being fixed inside the audit.

title: Tell the player what the run cost, not only what it did
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (75)', second entry. PLAYER-FACING.

RunSummary.summary_rows() (game/run_summary.gd:235-249) reports waves survived, pests defeated, time in the garden, threat reached, garden lost, compost swept and where you held them. Not one row is about seeds.

SeedBank.seeds_earned_total (game/seed_bank.gd:69) has been tracked all along and reaches no screen. A run where you scraped by on 40 seeds and one where you finished sitting on 300 unspent read identically on the card, and 'did I over-build or under-build' is the single question a post-mortem is for. There is no seeds_spent_total, but it is seeds_earned_total minus what is left, which the card already has access to.

Blocked by geometry, not by data: the card is full. The seventh row foots at 448 against BUTTON_Y 476 and an eighth would foot at 486, below the buttons (game/run_summary.gd:77). See -x for computing that ceiling instead of re-deriving it.

Consider folding rather than adding, the way beds_text folded escape evidence into the row that already counts escapes: 'Compost swept' is already an economy row and could carry earned-versus-spent without an eighth line.

ACCEPTANCE: the card says something about the run's economy; the row count still fits with the button clearance intact; a test asserts the number against a driven run rather than against a hand-built stats dictionary.

title: Look for the seam pattern in the other three gated subsystems
description:
SOURCE: log-devtools.md cycle 74, the no-gaps note. OUTSIDE this cycle work by construction -- it is a sweep, not a feature.

Twice in three cycles the useful assertion had to move to a seam rather than be strengthened in place, both times because the behaviour lives past a gate that is false for the entire headless suite: GardenTheme.animations_enabled() in cycle 71 (Plant.breathe_scale) and Sfx.should_play in cycle 74 (Sfx.tune_voice). Both were retrofitted after watching a mutation survive, which is the right order but a slow one.

The sweep: find every gate of that shape in game/ and ask, per gated block, whether anything past it is asserted at all. Known gates to start from are animations_enabled(), Sfx.should_play / audio_enabled, Music.should_play, and is_headless() -- but derive the list rather than trusting that sentence, since a census of mine has come up short three times in five cycles.

This is a REPORT, not a refactor. Extracting seams pre-emptively is explicitly warned against in .claude/skills/extract-a-testable-seam: the surviving mutation is the evidence that the extraction is load-bearing. So the deliverable is a list of gated blocks with a verdict each -- asserted, unassertable, or worth a mutation to find out.

ACCEPTANCE: every gate found is named with its file:line and a verdict; any block judged worth testing gets its own bead with the mutation that would prove it.

title: Assert the pitch scale's direction, not just one pair of it
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (74)', second entry.

Sfx.PITCH states a rule in prose: losses go lower, gains go higher, the routine half of a pair keeps the base, magnitudes graded by how grave the event is. test_tuning_a_voice_applies_both_axes_the_table_declares checks one of the five entries against one neighbour. The rest is prose, and this project has sixty pages of evidence about prose.

It is derivable. Every id in PITCH is one half of a pair that shares a SOUNDS file, so the check writes itself: find the partner by file, assert the sign of the difference matches whether the event is a loss or a gain, and assert the gravest loss sits furthest from 1.0. That is enumerate-the-pairs on a table that is literally pairs.

The one judgement call to make explicit rather than encode: which events count as losses. Do not hand-write that list in the test -- if the direction is real, it belongs beside the entries in PITCH, the way the WAVE_CLEARED reuse justification lives beside its SOUNDS entry.

ACCEPTANCE: adding a sixth PITCH entry pointing the wrong way fails; the loss/gain classification lives in game/sfx.gd, not in the test.

title: Teach settle_read_check about a tree read after a kill
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (73)', third entry.

Cycle 73 measured it: a corpse survives its own kill by 18 process frames, against the 2 that UI_SETTLE_FRAMES pumps (tools/run_tests.gd:849). Ten .kill() call sites across test/unit/ sit in that window, and nothing stops the eleventh from asserting the node is gone a frame later and being confused by a corpse that is behaving correctly.

tools/settle_read_check.py already exists for exactly this shape of mistake -- a test reading a value the settle frames were still moving. A corpse is that, with a name. Extend it to flag a tree read (is_instance_valid, get_child_count, a group query) within a few frames of a .kill().

Follow the house-static-checker contract the other eight obey: stdlib only, parallel-safe, exit 0/1/2, a printed denominator, a NOT COVERED line, a synthetic fixture AND a mutation of the checker itself. Note the specific trap this one has: the rule is about ORDER within a function, so scope by function rather than by file, and accept a waiver only if it says why.

ACCEPTANCE: the checker fires on a synthetic bad case and not on the ten real ones (or fires on a real one that turns out to be a genuine bug, which is a better outcome); the mutation pass is recorded.

title: Let a hard-won kill linger longer than an easy one
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (73)', second entry. PLAYER-FACING.

DEATH_LINGER is a flat 0.35s for every pest (game/pest.gd:200). corpse_rotation() and corpse_scale() vary by CAUSE -- a Chomp bite squashes, a seed bomb tilts -- so a corpse says how a pest died and never what died. An armoured beetle that soaked four volleys leaves on the same beat as an aphid that took one.

The game already believes harder kills are worth more. husk_multiplier() (game/pest.gd:928) pays a premium per mutation, and WaveDirector weather payout is the same idea one level up. The corpse is the one place that idea is missing, and it is the place the player actually looks.

Scaling DEATH_LINGER by husk_multiplier() is one line. Watch two things: DEATH_FADE is subtracted from DEATH_LINGER in the animated branch (game/pest.gd:877), so a scaled linger must keep the fade a tail rather than swallowing it; and cycle 73 measured a corpse surviving its own kill by 18 process frames headless, so a longer linger lengthens that window and the tests that sit in it.

ACCEPTANCE: two pests of different difficulty killed in the same frame leave at visibly different times; the fade stays a tail; test_a_pest_killed_headless_is_eventually_freed still passes with its bound.

title: Sweep bd descriptions for absence claims that never said how
description:
SOURCE: CLAUDE.md step 6, the rule added in cycle 72. OUTSIDE this cycle neighbourhood -- it is about the queue itself rather than about the game.

Three cycles running, an absence claim written into a bead description was wrong: -e1u3 said no plant has idle motion (the enumeration was of create_tween sites, and both animations are _process sinusoids) and -4lnu said step-time --then-pause had never been used in 71 cycles (log-devtools.md:3378 records it). Both were written in the same breath as filing the item, and both were believed a cycle later by the person who claimed them.

Step 3 citation rules now apply to descriptions. This is the retrospective half: go through the open beads for sentences of the form nothing does X, there is no Y, this is not built, and check whether the description says HOW that was established. Where it does not, either establish it or soften the sentence.

Do not close beads wholesale on this sweep. A description that overstates its evidence is not the same as a bead that is wrong, and kanban-staleness-audit bar applies: a wrong deletion loses an idea nobody will have again.

ACCEPTANCE: every open bead whose description asserts an absence either names the search that established it or is reworded to say it is unverified; the count of each is reported.

title: Assert a flourish reaches its peak, now that a sub-second tween is walkable
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (72)', third entry.

Four flourishes are written to reach distinct extremes -- the cob recoil (0.88, 1.14) at game/corn_cobbler.gd:183, the Chomp bite (1.18, 0.82) at game/chomp_flower.gd:155, the upgrade (0.72, 1.34) at game/corn_cobbler.gd:331, the planting pop (1.12, 1.12) at game/plant.gd:272 -- and the extreme is the entire content of each. Nothing asserts any of them; the tests assert start and end, both Vector2.ONE.

Until cycle 72 that was not observable. A 0.15s tween is shorter than a bus round-trip and four consecutive polls all return the landed value, which is indistinguishable from a tween that never ran. The walk recipe in .claude/skills/read-a-moving-value/SKILL.md makes it deterministic: pause BEFORE creating the tween, then step-time --seconds 0.03 --then-pause.

Note the sampling caveat this bead exists to settle: a stepped walk of the recoil reached 0.900 against a written 0.88. That is probably the 0.03s grid straddling the peak rather than a discrepancy, and a finer step would say which. Do not assert equality with the written constant until that is known -- assert the direction and the magnitude first.

ACCEPTANCE: one flourish has a runtime check that its peak is reached, with the step size chosen from a measurement rather than guessed; the finding about 0.900 versus 0.88 is resolved either way.

title: Audit the rest of the 'Requested directly by James' list the way two of them just were
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md, 'Requested directly by James -- not grown, asked for'. OUTSIDE this cycle's neighbourhood by the workflow rule, and it is the section with the worst measured accuracy in the file.

Two of its bullets have now been checked against the code and BOTH were substantially wrong:
  - 'More waves, and bosses' claimed the table ends at 8 waves and there is no boss. The table runs past 16 (game/wave_director.gd:164, and its own prose at :90 and :155) and a boss mechanic ships (game/game.gd:796). Filed as -35mu.
  - 'Animate all the plants and enemies' claimed plants and pests are mostly static art. Plant._wobble (game/plant.gd:351) and Pest._gait (game/pest.gd:733) have both existed since the first playable build. Corrected in place in cycle 71.

That is two for two. The remaining bullets -- idle animation's 'twitch', the epic-tier animated dandelion, enemy facing direction -- have not been checked, and facing in particular has a test whose name suggests it shipped (test_update_facing_maps_every_cardinal_to_the_art_up_screen_convention).

This section is the user's own words, so a wrong STALE here is the most expensive kind. Use kanban-staleness-audit's bar: open the implementing code, not the tests, and re-derive any number.

ACCEPTANCE: a verdict per remaining bullet with the evidence column filled before the verdict column; DRIFTED entries rewritten in place with citations, the way this cycle rewrote the animation one.

title: Rotate the sway about the stem instead of the middle
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (71)', second entry.

_sway_pivot (game/plant.gd) rotates about the sprite centre, so a plant wobbles around its middle like a tethered balloon rather than bending at the stem. Moving _sprite.offset down 32 px and the pivot up by the same amount rotates about the base at no runtime cost.

This was not worth attempting before cycle 71 because the planting pop and every other flourish shared the sprite transform, so changing its anchor changed how five animations looked. Now the event tweens live on the sprite and the sway lives on the pivot, so this touches only the pivot.

Note the interaction with -gfpj: moving the sprite's offset moves the art relative to the cues that _draw() paints in the PLANT's space, which is the same relationship that bead is already going to photograph.

ACCEPTANCE: a screenshot before and after; the planting pop is unchanged; the muzzle fan still lands where the cob's shoulder is.

title: Point the muzzle fan at the current target, not the last one
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (70)', third entry. PLAYER-FACING.

Two plants draw where they will act next and both only after they have already acted. The cob's fan follows _aim_angle, set inside _fire_at (game/corn_cobbler.gd:119); the Dandelion's blast circle sits on _last_landing, set inside its own fire path (game/dandelion.gd:234) behind a _has_fired gate (:378).

Both are post-views wearing the shape of a preview. A freshly planted cob points wherever _aim_angle was initialised until its first shot; a Dandelion shows nothing at all. The information a player wants BEFORE committing seeds -- which way will this thing shoot -- exists in both plants one frame after it stops being useful.

The cob is the cheap half: _act already calls _furthest_along_in_range(pests, RANGE) every tick (game/corn_cobbler.gd:109), so aiming the idle fan at that target costs no new work, just an assignment outside the fire branch. Watch the redraw budget -- _aim_angle changes would now queue_redraw on every tick a target moves, which is what READINESS_STEPS exists to bound for the fade.

The Dandelion half is a separate decision and probably a separate bead: it has no continuous target, so a preview means predicting a landing spot before the volley opens.

ACCEPTANCE: a cob with a pest in range points at it before firing; a test asserts the fan angle tracks the chosen target without a shot having been taken; the redraw rate is measured, not assumed.

title: OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md filed a real cue under 'sprites drawing themselves'
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (69)', third entry. Found one cycle after the document was written.

game/OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md:55-56 lists husk_layer.gd among the files that are art rather than cues. But game/husk_layer.gd:69-77 draws draw_arc(..., TAU * frac, ...) whose sweep IS the husk's remaining life -- a mark that carries state, which is the table's own definition of a cue.

Including it supplies the row the table is missing, PARTIAL ARC = TIME REMAINING, and that demotes chomp_flower.gd:138's shrinking ring from a lone exception to one instance of a vocabulary the game already has.

The exclusion list is where the correction was hiding, which is worth noting in the document itself: a derivation is only as good as its filter, and the filter was the one part written from judgement rather than from grep.

ACCEPTANCE: the table has the new row with both instances cited; the exceptions section is re-read in light of it; the test that pins the mechanical half covers whatever of it is numeric.

title: Make 'only one line may carry a deadline' fail instead of merely warning
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (69)', second entry.

game/hud.gd:347 warns that two MESSAGE_DEADLINE lines cannot defer each other -- whichever waits is wrong by construction -- and game/game.gd:1333 is today the only producer. Enumeration: grep -rn MESSAGE_DEADLINE game/ returns the constant at hud.gd:351, one comment at game.gd:1330 and that one call.

The person who adds the second producer will be reading their own feature, not this constant. A test asserting the call-site count is exactly one, failing WITH THE PARAGRAPH as its message, puts the warning in front of them at the moment it applies. Same move message_corpus_check already makes for the row's strings, and cheaper -- this is a grep over game/, not a checker.

ACCEPTANCE: adding a second MESSAGE_DEADLINE call site fails a gate whose message is the design argument, not a count.

title: Give the lane-pressure hatch a row in the grammar table
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (68)', third entry.

lane_pressure_overlay.gd:96 draws hatched lines carrying TWO channels on one mark -- the angle says aimed-versus-unaimed, the alpha says how much pressure a cell took. It is the most sophisticated cue in the game and it is the only one absent from OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md's table.

It was left out because it is drawn on the board rather than on a node, which is a real difference and a bad reason -- a grammar that omits its best example teaches less than one that explains why that example is different.

That file's own header already argues at length about why an angle and not a colour, and why density was rejected. Most of the row is already written; it needs lifting into the table with a note that board-drawn cues have channels node-drawn ones do not.

ACCEPTANCE: the table covers every cue in the game, with board-drawn versus node-drawn stated as the axis it turns on.

title: Give the Chomp's chew ring a shape that is not a range
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (68)', second entry. PLAYER-FACING.

chomp_flower.gd:138 shrinks a solid ring as a chew completes -- a progress bar in ring form. It shares its shape with the four rings that mean 'this is how far I act', so a player who learned 'solid ring = reach' from three plants meets a fourth where it means TIME.

Cycle 68 documented it as an exception in OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md, which is honest and is not the same as legible.

The grammar already has an unused shape that fits: a DASHED ring is a remark about the thing inside it, and a chew IS a remark about the pest being held. Alternatively an arc sweep (a clock hand rather than a shrinking circle) reads as time in a way no full circle does.

ACCEPTANCE: the chew cue is distinguishable from a reach ring with colour discarded; OVERLAY_GRAMMAR.md loses one of its two exceptions.

title: Ask whether the budget ratchet should keep a reserve
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (67)', third entry. A DESIGN QUESTION about the budget system itself.

Three rows are at floor because each was ratcheted down in the commit that spent it. Every one of those was the correct local move -- the floor should reflect what was measured -- and they add up to a HUD with no slack that nobody chose.

hud_message_row's 121px against a floor of 40 is the only room left, and it exists only because nobody has ratcheted it yet. So the current state is an accident of which budgets happened to be tightened.

The question: should a floor be set at the MEASUREMENT, or at measurement plus a reserve? A reserve makes spending the last of a row require moving a number that says 'reserve', which is a decision rather than a default. It also makes the floor less honest as a record of what was measured, which is what it is for today.

Decide once and write the answer into BUDGET_FLOOR's header either way.

ACCEPTANCE: a recorded decision with reasoning; if reserves ship, the existing floors are re-derived under the new rule.

title: Give the message row's slack a name, or stop treating it as the slack fund
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (66)', second entry.

hud_message_row holds 121px against a floor of 40 -- the only budget with real room. Every other HUD row is at its floor. Cycle 61 spent 185px of that slack on a one-shot tutorial tip, correctly and within budget.

The consequence is structural rather than a bug: any future 'just add a short line' lands on the message row, because it is the only place that can absorb one. That will keep being true until the row is full, at which point the HUD has nowhere at all.

Two honest options. Either name it -- write in BUDGET_FLOOR's header that this row is deliberately the HUD's slack and that spending it is a decision, not a default. Or reclaim room elsewhere so the pressure is not all on one row.

ACCEPTANCE: a decision recorded; if the row keeps the role, its header says so.

title: Watch for evidence strings that name a surface rather than a corpus
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (66)', third entry.

hud_readouts' evidence string read 'Font.get_string_size() over each live readout in Root/TopBar/StatsRow'. That parses as measuring the CURRENT text -- a budget that passes because the counter happens to say 'Seeds 25' today. It actually sweeps Hud.WORST_CASE_TEXT against each readout's live SLOT (game/game.gd:2203). Corrected in cycle 66, after I misread it myself.

The general shape: an evidence string that names the SURFACE is ambiguous about whether the worst case or the current value was measured, and those differ by everything. A string naming the CORPUS cannot be misread that way.

This is scope-vs-claim shape 1 with a twist -- the string was not stale, it was AMBIGUOUS, which no staleness check would catch. Read all seven with that specific question: does this name what was measured, or only where?

ACCEPTANCE: every evidence string names its corpus; any that names only a surface is rewritten.

title: Show that a pest was fought and survived, not just that it got through
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (65)', second entry.

Pest._ever_engaged (game/pest.gd:796, and :646 when a mouth holds one) is set by any damage above zero. The run summary already counts pests that 'walked in untouched'.

So the game knows the difference between a pest that strolled past an empty road and one that was shot at, slowed, bitten and got through anyway -- and the player only ever sees that as an aggregate at the end of the run, if at all. Those are different stories about the same lost bed: one says 'you had no answer there', the other says 'your answer was not enough'.

Overlaps -above (marking an escape): if an escape gets a cue at all, this flag is what should shade it. Do them together or the second will want to change the first.

ACCEPTANCE: an escape distinguishes fought-and-survived from untouched; a test drives both.
notes: Cycle 66 changes this bead's footing: the escape is NOT unmarked (sound + lane tint + readout punch all fire), so this is no longer 'add a cue to a silent event' but 'shade an existing cue with information the game already has'. _ever_engaged is still unshown, which is the real remainder. The sibling -tuos was closed as already-shipped.

title: Give the kernel kill a knockback, or decide the plain corpse is the point
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (65)', first entry. A DECISION before a change.

Cycle 65 made a bitten corpse narrower and a blasted one tilted, and left the kernel kill on the straight default deliberately -- so the two that differ read as remarkable. But a Corn Cobbler is the plant most players own most of the time, so the MAJORITY of corpses now carry no information.

A kernel arrives with a direction (Kernel._physics_process flies until it leaves the board), so a small knockback along that travel is available. It costs one argument, where the two shipped cues needed none.

The real question is whether 'the plain corpse is the common case' is worth more than 'every death says something'. Both are defensible and the current state is the result of picking the first. Decide on purpose rather than by accretion.

ACCEPTANCE: a decision recorded with its reasoning; if knockback ships, the straight corpse keeps at least one path so the existing test stays meaningful.

title: Give kanban a top-of-file index of its sections
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md's size, made obvious by this cycle's audit.

The file is 2560 lines and its own top says roughly half is stale. There is no way to see what sections exist without grepping, which is why the oldest three sat unaudited for 64 cycles and why two numbering runs coexisted unnoticed.

A short index at the top -- section name, line, one-line summary, last audited cycle -- makes 'what have we never looked at' answerable at a glance. The 'last audited' column is the one that matters: it turns staleness from a property nobody can see into a column that sorts.

Keep it generated rather than hand-maintained if that is cheap (the headings are regular), because a hand-maintained index of a file about stale hand-maintained lists would be its own joke.

ACCEPTANCE: the index exists, names every section, and records when each was last audited.

title: Sweep kanban for other duplicate section headings
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's near-miss.

`### New this cycle (25 of 30)` appears twice with different subtitles, so `uniq -d` on the full heading lines finds nothing while a prefix match finds two. Cycle 64's first cut matched the earlier one and removed 1937 lines instead of 85; git diff --stat before the commit is what caught it.

The file is 2560 lines with ~60 section headings written across 64 cycles by a process that numbers them inconsistently. Cheap to check: group headings by their bracketed prefix rather than the whole line, and report any prefix with more than one.

If there are more collisions, renaming them is worth more than remembering the rule -- a heading that is unique cannot be cut wrongly.

ACCEPTANCE: every section heading prefix is unique, or the duplicates are listed with a note beside each.

title: Give the run summary the corpus pattern
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (63)', second entry.

Hud.message_corpus() is now the only place in the game that enumerates its own output: one function listing every string a surface can show, beside the code that produces them, read by BOTH the budget and a checker. Three cycles of defects went into arriving at it.

game/run_summary.gd builds seven rows of text with no equivalent. It has a clearance gate (test_combat.gd measures the last row's foot against the replay button) and nothing at all about content -- so a row whose value string grows is caught only if it happens to push the layout.

The pattern is cheap to copy and the checker generalises: the corpus checker is already parameterised by CORPUS_FUNC and the call token, so a second surface may need configuration rather than a second tool. Check that before writing one -- a second copy is what this cycle spent its time undoing inside the checker itself.

ACCEPTANCE: the summary's strings are enumerated in one place read by its own budget; the existing clearance gate still passes.

title: Audit the five house checkers that predate the fixture discipline
description:
SOURCE: step 0, and cycle 62's experience writing a rule into an existing checker. DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THIS CYCLE'S NEIGHBOURHOOD in kind -- this reads old tools rather than extending the one just touched.

message_corpus_check and mirror_check both carry their fixture cases and mutation lists in their docstrings, because both were written after house-static-checker existed. The older ones -- world_control_check, meta_key_check, group_leak_check, svg_style_check, settle_read_check -- were written before or during that skill's development.

The question is not whether they work. It is whether anyone has watched them FAIL, and whether that is written down where the next person editing one will see it. house-static-checker's own words: 'a checker that has never been observed to fail is not a checker'.

Expect some to have been mutated already and simply not to say so. Recording that is most of the value.

ACCEPTANCE: each of the five names its fixture cases and its mutation results in its docstring, or gains them.
notes: Cycle 63 proved the concrete hazard: adding a rule to message_corpus_check broke that checker's own two older fixtures, and neither was wrong -- minimal stubs violate new rules by construction. When auditing each checker, run ALL its fixtures, not just the one for the rule being examined.

title: Report the worst RECURRING string beside the worst possible one
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (61)', second entry.

cmd budgets reports the message row at 755 of 876 px. That is the right number -- the budget prices the ceiling the format allows -- and it is a misleading one to plan with, because the string setting it is a first-arm prompt seen once per save. The row is at 86% of capacity for something almost no session displays.

Cycle 61 wrote an acceptance criterion ('budgets returns to ~570') that was wrong for exactly this reason, which is evidence the single number invites the mistake.

Game.budget_entries() already returns dictionaries, so a second measurement is a field rather than a rework: the widest string excluding one-shots. Then a reader can judge whether 121px of headroom is comfortable.

Careful: the FLOOR must stay against the true ceiling. A recurring-case number is for judgement, not for gating, or the one-shot string stops being priced at all.

ACCEPTANCE: budgets reports both; the floor still gates on the ceiling.

title: Decide what bounds a plant's display name now the row's worst case is a tip
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (60)', second entry.

Before cycle 60 the widest string the message row held was the wave prep note -- a game event. It is now the armed-uproot prompt for a Bomb Dandelion, which is a TUTORIAL string.

So every plant added from here is measured against a sentence that exists to teach rather than to report, and a plant with a long name will be refused by a tip. That is a strange constraint to discover from a budget failure months later.

Either cap display names explicitly (with the cap stated where names are declared, in PlantCatalog), or move the tip out of the recurring message -- which is -j80m's follow-up above and would resolve this as a side effect. Do that one FIRST and re-check whether this is still a problem.

ACCEPTANCE: the binding constraint on a display name is written down where names are declared, whatever it turns out to be.

title: Make the preview's subject a named predicate
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (59)', third entry.

_update_preview (game/game.gd:1569) now decides two things: which cell the hover is over, and -- since cycle 59 -- which PLANT the hover is about. The second is three lines of subject-selection at the top of a function whose name promises only the first.

It is fine at two modes and it is exactly where a third would go in badly. This file's own pattern is a named predicate (new_cover_cells, ring_color, shows_dead_zone) precisely so a rule can be read and tested without a canvas.

previewing_plant() -> StringName, with the armed-move rule in its header, is the same refactor those three already had.

ACCEPTANCE: the subject rule is a predicate with its own test; _update_preview reads it.

title: Teach house-static-checker that an improvement and a regression must be printed together
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's step 4 reflection.

suite_reach_check printed 'PROGRESS: 2 baselined symbols are now named by a test. Re-run --baseline-write' AND '1 NEW' in the same output. Acting on the PROGRESS line alone -- which is what it invites -- would have banked a regression under an improvement, since --baseline-write rewrites the whole file.

It was legible only because both numbers appear together. A tool that reported just 'you improved, re-bank' would have been actively harmful.

That generalises: house-static-checker already demands a printed denominator so a clean result cannot hide an empty input. The same argument applies to any tool that invites an ACTION -- if acting on one number could bury another, print both at the point of invitation. Add it beside the denominator rule.

ACCEPTANCE: the skill states it, citing suite_reach_check's PROGRESS/NEW pairing as the worked example.
close_reason: Done in the same cycle it was filed -- house-static-checker now carries 'if acting on one number could bury another, print both at the point of invitation', citing suite_reach_check's PROGRESS/NEW pairing.

title: Draw the difference between two cobs at different levels
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (58)', third entry. PLAYER-FACING.

Every cue built so far answers a SPATIAL question -- the rings, the dots, the dead-ground bar. A plant's rate is invisible until selected and read as text (game/hud.gd:1154 prints damage and interval for a cob).

So two cobs covering identical cells at different upgrade levels look identical on the board. That is exactly the shape of gap that made the coverage-versus-engagement work necessary over cycles 54-57, and the same fix applies: draw the thing that differs.

The muzzle fan already exists and already fades with cooldown (CornCobbler._draw_muzzle_fan), so there is a rate-shaped cue on the plant already -- it may only need to scale with level rather than needing a new overlay.

ACCEPTANCE: two cobs at different levels are distinguishable without selecting either; a screenshot proves it.
close_reason: Already shipped in cycle 58 (muzzle_pips varies with level); the missing half was the acceptance evidence. Measured on the live board with pixel sampling: level 1 = one pip, level 3 = five pips plus a spread arc, distinguishable at a glance. The run also produced a surviving mutation, fixed in 9a9e203.

title: Show the replant cost beside the uproot refund
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (58)', second entry. PLAYER-FACING.

The uproot button reads `Uproot (+%d)` (game/hud.gd:1209) -- what you get back. Nothing says what putting the plant back costs, though both numbers are known constants for every catalogue entry.

'Uproot +12, replant 20' is a subtraction the game could do and currently leaves to the player mid-decision on a four-second timer.

BLOCKED-ISH on -r722: the selection panel has no room (cycle 57 measured the cob's second line at ~190px of a 232px box, and the VBox runs to within 16px of the panel foot), and the uproot button's text is the only string there with slack. Measure before writing -- `Really uproot? (+99)` is already the longest state that button takes.

ACCEPTANCE: the net cost is visible while deciding; the button's worst-case string is measured and fits.

title: Audit the design brief's UI claims against three cycles of new cues
description:
SOURCE: the design brief. DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THIS CYCLE'S NEIGHBOURHOOD in kind -- cycles 55-57 wrote drawing code, this reads a document.

Three new visual cues have shipped in three cycles and the brief predates all of them. If it describes what the player can see, it is now describing a smaller game than the one that exists.

NOTE the neighbours: -hwo6 audits STYLE.md (the art conventions) and -w0wh audits the brief's COMBAT claims. This is the brief's UI claims specifically, which neither covers. If they turn out to overlap once opened, fold rather than duplicate -- per step 6, note the open bead instead of filing a second.

ACCEPTANCE: a per-claim verdict for the brief's UI section, file:line for anything marked shipped.
notes: Cycle 58 widened the gap again: a fifth cue state shipped (the armed sole-cover rings). Four cycles of new UI now postdate the brief.

title: Re-run the budget verbs now that two cues have been added
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's step 4 reflection.

Cycles 55, 56 and 57 added PlacementPreview's new-cover dots, SoleCoverMarks' rings and the holds-nothing ring. None of them touched a budgeted coupling, so `cmd budgets` has not been read since cycle 52 -- and cycle 52's whole lesson was that a budget over a subset reports more headroom than exists.

This is a ten-minute check, not a feature: launch, `cmd budgets`, read all five, confirm each still describes what it sweeps. scope-vs-claim's shape 1 applied on a schedule rather than on suspicion.

ACCEPTANCE: a written verdict per budget; anything whose evidence string no longer matches its corpus is corrected.
close_reason: All seven budgets re-read (not five -- the note was stale). 0 regressions. Three sit exactly at their declared floor by ratchet, so any spend there fires immediately; hud_message_row holds the only slack. hud_readouts' evidence string was ambiguous about whether it measures live text or the declared worst case, and is corrected.

title: Keep the previous selection's rings while comparing two plants
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (57)', second entry. PLAYER-FACING.

Selecting a plant rings what it alone holds; selecting another replaces those rings. The question a player actually has is comparative -- 'which of these two should I move?' -- and answering it currently means clicking back and forth and holding two pictures in your head.

Game.sole_cover_cells() already computes per plant, so a held modifier that keeps the previous selection's marks on screen needs no new computation, only a second SoleCoverMarks kept visible.

Careful: two ring sets in the same colour would be unreadable, and this project's two-channel rule means the second set needs a shape or a dash pattern rather than only a different hue. See -iqf2, which is already asking what the hover dots and the selection rings look like together -- do that first.

ACCEPTANCE: two plants' sole-cover sets are legible at once; a screenshot proves it.

title: Read the design brief's combat claims against the coverage system
description:
SOURCE: the design brief. DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THIS CYCLE'S NEIGHBOURHOOD in subject, though it touches the same system -- cycle 55 was UI cues, this is the document.

Five cycles have now produced measurements the brief predates: coverage is not engagement (a cob fires at one pest), a minimal cover loses pests a redundant one stops, dead ground differs per plant and moved in opposite directions when the road changed, and the road's paint is out of channels.

If the brief describes coverage as a solved or simple idea, it is now describing something the game does not do. Audit just its combat and coverage claims -- not the whole document, which is -hwo6's larger job -- and cite file:line for anything marked shipped, per kanban-staleness-audit's bar.

ACCEPTANCE: a per-claim verdict for the brief's combat section.

title: Teach kanban-staleness-audit the derive-vs-record question
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's step 5 reflection.

Cycle 54 set out to derive five recorded road figures and correctly derived only two. The deciding question was derive-the-list's: is the membership a RULE or a TASTE CALL? The walled mouth list is a rule ('one beside every road cell'). Seven cobs is a taste call ('enough firepower'), and deriving it produced a better cover, a weaker garden, and two broken tests.

That question generalises past lists to the whole backlog: a kanban entry proposing to 'automate' or 'derive' something needs it asked BEFORE the work, not after. It is the cheapest possible staleness check and it is not in the audit skill.

ACCEPTANCE: kanban-staleness-audit names the rule-vs-taste-call question and cites cycle 54 as the case where deriving was measurably the wrong call.

title: Surface dead ground before the player is holding a plant
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (54)', third entry. PLAYER-FACING.

The dead-ground cue is per-plant and appears at placement time. So a player scanning the board to decide WHAT to buy sees uniform grass, and only learns a corner is useless after committing to a plant.

Cycle 53 sharpened this: the reshape moved Corn dead ground 15 -> 11 and Chomp 34 -> 36, in OPPOSITE directions. A player who learned 'the top-right is useless' on one board has learned something false about the next.

Overlaps -g8kc (tint ground no plant can use), which is the always-true subset. This one is the harder, more useful version: show the currently-SELECTED plant's dead ground on hover over the shop entry, before purchase.

ACCEPTANCE: hovering a shop entry previews that plant's dead ground on the board; a test asserts the preview matches PlacementPreview's own answer for that plant.

title: Show a par score for garden efficiency on the run summary
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (54)', second entry. PLAYER-FACING.

test_combat.gd's _cover_greedily now computes the SMALLEST garden reaching every road cell -- five cobs on the current road. That number is a genuinely interesting thing to know and it already computes.

The player currently gets no signal about whether their garden was efficient or merely large. game/run_summary.gd is where a par would land: 'you held the road with 11 plants; 5 would have reached it'. It reframes a won run as a puzzle with a better answer, which is the cheapest replay motivation available.

Careful: reaching every cell is NOT the same as holding the road -- that is exactly what cycle 54 found, since the minimal cover loses pests the redundant one stops. So the par must be described as REACH, not as a garden that would have won, or it teaches something false.

ACCEPTANCE: the summary shows a reach-par; its wording distinguishes reach from sufficiency; a test asserts the par against a known road.
notes: Cycle 55 strengthens the case: test_combat's _cover_greedily now computes the minimal garden reaching every road cell, so the par number is already written and tested rather than needing to be invented. -f909 was filed as a duplicate note and closed.

title: Tint ground no plant in the catalogue can use
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (53)', third entry. PLAYER-FACING.

The reshape opened bigger clearings: the Chomp's 74 px grab radius now strands 36 of 94 buildable cells, up from 34, while the Corn's 176 px ring strands only 11. The dead-ground cue is per-plant and appears at placement time, so a player scanning the board before choosing a plant sees uniform grass.

Ground that NO plant in the catalogue can use is different in kind -- it is scenery, permanently -- and a faint permanent tint would say so without teaching anything false about the per-plant cue. The count is small: cells dead for the LONGEST reach in the catalogue.

Careful: this number changes when a plant with a longer reach is unlocked or added, so it must be derived from PlantCatalog rather than recorded, and it should probably consider only plants the player has actually unlocked.

ACCEPTANCE: the tint is derived from the catalogue's maximum reach, updates when a plant unlocks, and is asserted by a test that adds a longer-reach plant and watches it shrink.

title: Show when a covered cell is covered by a plant that is already busy
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (53)', second entry. PLAYER-FACING.

Six cobs reach all 32 road cells and a pest still crossed unfought, because _furthest_along_in_range (game/corn_cobbler.gd:109) picks exactly ONE target. The board's coverage cue tells a player a cell is covered; it cannot tell them the plant covering it is permanently committed elsewhere.

That gap is measured already -- the over-promise tests count 'unanswered' stays on covered ground and the figure is large (65% in one recorded run). So the data exists and only the cue is missing.

Design care needed: this must not read as 'the cell is uncovered', which is false, and it must not fire constantly during a heavy wave, which would make it noise. A second tint or a hatch on covered-but-contested ground, shown only while a wave runs.

ACCEPTANCE: a player can tell 'covered' from 'covered and contested' at a glance, and a test drives a wave and asserts the cue appears on the cells the over-promise run identifies.

title: Audit the design brief against what the game actually does
description:
SOURCE: step 0's third pre-flight item plus the design brief. DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THIS CYCLE'S NEIGHBOURHOOD -- cycle 52 was entirely the HUD message row and tooling.

scope-vs-claim's four shapes are all about a CHECK describing itself. The same asymmetry applies to a design document: it states what the game is, nothing compares that to what the game does, and the prose is what a reader trusts.

The brief has never been audited. Cycles 49-52 have found that a user-requested feature already shipped (facing direction), that kanban's Done section has never been read back, and that a standing note in cycle-log.md was wrong about a number -- all the same shape. The brief is the largest unaudited claim surface left.

Use kanban-staleness-audit's bar: before writing that something is missing, open the code that would contain it. Expect a third of it to be shipped, a third stale, a third still real -- and the value is in knowing which.

ACCEPTANCE: a per-claim verdict with file:line for anything marked shipped.

title: Gather the message-corpus waiver reasons into one place
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (52)', third entry.

The five `# message-corpus-check: ok - <reason>` waivers (game/game.gd:231, :1397, :1464, :1468, :1605) are collectively the best documentation of what the message row can show that cannot be priced statically. Each says something true and non-obvious.

But the answer to 'what can the row show that we cannot measure?' is now assembled by grep -- which is EXACTLY the failure the corpus just fixed one level down, reappearing in the waivers that made the fix possible.

Cheapest fix: have message_corpus_check print the waived sites AND their reasons on a clean run, not just the count. The information is already parsed; it is one line per waiver, and it turns a grep into an output.

ACCEPTANCE: a clean run names each waived site and its reason.
notes: Cycle 62 added a SIXTH waiver of a different kind -- a bool-variant waiver in hud.gd, not a call-site waiver in game.gd. Include both kinds in the clean-run output, or 'what does this checker deliberately not price?' stays a grep across two files.

title: Derive message durations from length instead of picking six numbers
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (52)', second entry. PLAYER-FACING.

show_message() durations are hand-picked and unrelated: 8.0s opening hint (game/game.gd:264), 6.0s wave cleared (:415), 4.0s eaten (:1197), 5.0s packet (:1407), 2.5s mute and colourblind (:1464, :1484), 2.0s uproot cancelled and husk swept (:1319, :1588).

The spread is probably RIGHT -- a message you must read to act on should outlast a confirmation -- but nothing states the rule, so the next message added gets a number by vibes. Reading time scales with length, and Hud.message_corpus() now knows every length.

A duration derived from character count with a floor and a ceiling would make 8.0 and 2.0 consequences of one decision rather than eight independent ones. Keep an explicit override for anything that genuinely needs to outlast its length.

ACCEPTANCE: durations come from one function; every current value is either reproduced by it or carries a written reason for its override.
notes: Cycle 62 lowers the cost: Hud.message_corpus() now knows every message's text, so 'reading time scales with length' is a two-line change against the corpus rather than a survey of fifteen call sites.

title: Audit STYLE.md's claims against the art the way the budgets were audited
description:
SOURCE: step 0's third pre-flight item, applying scope-vs-claim. DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THIS CYCLE'S NEIGHBOURHOOD -- cycle 51 was budgets, tests and skills.

art_src/STYLE.md states conventions the art is supposed to obey; line 14 says facing is up-screen (-Y) for anything directional. Cycle 50 checked that claim against the three pest SVGs by hand and it held. Nobody has checked its OTHER claims against the other sixteen SVGs.

This is scope-vs-claim shape 1 at repo scale: a document states a scope ('anything directional') and nothing compares it to what exists. svg_style_check.py already parses the art for palette conformance, so there is a place to put whatever turns out to be mechanically checkable.

ACCEPTANCE: a per-claim verdict for STYLE.md; anything checkable moved into svg_style_check.py with a fixture, anything not checkable narrowed in the prose so it stops implying a guarantee.
notes: Third piece of evidence (cycle 56): two new drawn cues shipped in cycles 55 and 56 -- PlacementPreview's new-cover dots and SoleCoverMarks' sole-cover rings -- and neither was checked against STYLE.md's conventions. -6v8n was filed as a duplicate note and closed.

title: Check whether the wave-cleared line eats the prep note's window
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (51)', third entry. PLAYER-FACING.

_paint_message_row gives a transient message precedence over the standing note (established in cycle 48, and correct). wave_cleared_line (game/hud.gd:1655) fires exactly when the prep note becomes relevant: at the end of a wave, when the player is deciding what to plant next.

So the question is whether the cleared line's duration overlaps the window in which someone reads the forecast. If it does, the player is told what just happened during the seconds they need to be told what is coming.

This is a design question and the precedence is deliberate -- do not 'fix' it by inverting the rule. Measure the overlap first: use pause + _message_left, per .claude/skills/read-a-moving-value.

ACCEPTANCE: a measured verdict on the overlap, and a decision recorded either way.

title: Kill pests differently depending on what killed them
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (50)', third entry. PLAYER-FACING JUICE, which this cycle and the two before it produced almost none of.

test_a_pest_killed_mid_stride_leaves_a_straight_corpse asserts a corpse lies on its facing with the gait lean undone -- a genuinely nice touch that already ships, and the hook is already there in Pest.kill(). Right now a Chomp bite, a Corn Cobbler kernel and a seed bomb all produce the same straight corpse.

Differentiating them is cheap on a system that already has the seam: a bite could leave a shorter corpse or a bitten-off angle, a kernel a knockback along its travel, a bomb a scatter. Keep the existing straight-corpse assertion true for at least one path so the test does not have to be rewritten wholesale.

ACCEPTANCE: at least two death sources produce visibly different corpses, each asserted.
close_reason: Corpses now differ by cause: bitten squashes across the body, blasted tilts off the facing, everything else stays straight (the default, so the two that differ read as remarkable). Five mutations killed. Chomp path driven end-to-end; seed_bomb.gd unreached at runtime and reported.

title: Gate the weather multipliers with assert_margin too
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (50)', second entry.

-frzz covers the pest gait constants. The weather multipliers have exactly the same shape and no bead: WEATHER_DROUGHT_SEED_BONUS (1.5) and WEATHER_RAIN_HEAL_FRACTION in game/wave_director.gd, both tuned, both with reasoning in prose, neither asserted against the corpus of values sitting near them.

_T.assert_margin(values, threshold, margin, recorded) exists for precisely this. A tuned constant with a documented justification and no test is a comment, not a contract -- and cycle 48 showed what that costs when the corpus a measurement claims drifts from the one it sweeps.

ACCEPTANCE: a test that fails if a weather multiplier moves close enough to 1.0 that the weather stops being distinguishable, or close enough to another weather's value that the two stop being different choices.

title: Add a level whose road climbs, exercising the -Y facing branch
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (50)', first entry, which came out of the runtime pass on -ymth.

Board._build_route() (game/board.gd:162) walks _path_order, and the shipped level's route -- read live off a pest, thirty-four points -- runs right, down, left, down, right. Not one -Y step. So Pest._update_facing()'s `_facing = 0.0` branch (game/pest.gd:679) has never executed in a real game.

A road that CLIMBS is the cheapest new-level variety available: the art already exists and rests up-screen, the code path already works and is now asserted (test_update_facing_maps_every_cardinal_to_the_art_up_screen_convention), and it makes the vertical axis mean something in both directions rather than only downward.

ACCEPTANCE: a level whose _path_order contains at least one upward step, and a pest observed on it rendering with rotation 0.
close_reason: Road reshaped to (0,1)-(6,1)-(6,4)-(2,4)-(2,7)-(9,7)-(9,3)-(13,3): climbs up column 9, holds 32 cells / 2112 px so no length-derived constant moved. Five shape-dependent tests re-derived. Confirmed on screen at _facing=0.0. dc3820f

title: Build screen-content-audit, or record why not
description:
SOURCE: step 0's second pre-flight item (skill ideas in log.md vs .claude/skills/).

log.md:3267 names it: 'given a screen and its content table, check that every entry resolves to a DISTINCT asset (by content hash, not path), that every text field is non-empty and within the box it is given, and that no two entries claim the same source.' Three defects in one session were that check at different angles -- a duplicate photograph, an ellipsised note, a kernel stretched from 32px to 190px -- and all three shipped in a table that read as entirely correct.

ONE identification so far, so this is not yet at step 0's build-it bar. Filed to make the second identification land against something instead of being written down again. Cycle 45 established the good precedent here: decide NOT to build a checker when precision would be low, and record the measurement that says so. Either build it or write that measurement.

ACCEPTANCE: the skill exists, or a written count of how many real findings it would have produced against the screens this game actually has.

title: Gate the pest gait constants with assert_margin
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md, 'New this cycle (49)', third entry.

GAIT_SWING 0.13, GAIT_RATE 8.5, GAIT_REFERENCE_SPEED 60.0, GAIT_RATE_MIN 0.55, GAIT_RATE_MAX 1.9 (game/pest.gd:235-245). The header gives real reasoning for the reference speed -- between the aphid's 78 and the beetle's 38, so the fast one scuttles and the slow one plods without a per-species constant -- and nothing asserts it.

That reasoning is exactly what _T.assert_margin(values, threshold, margin, recorded) gates: it checks the corpus items sitting near a tuned value. A species added at speed 61 would land on the boundary silently today.

ACCEPTANCE: a test that fails when a species' speed is close enough to GAIT_REFERENCE_SPEED that the constant's stated justification no longer holds.

title: Audit the six oldest kanban sections against the code they claim about
description:
SOURCE: step 0's third backlog (kanban.md), which says at its own top that the historical sections are unpruned and roughly half stale.

DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THIS CYCLE'S NEIGHBOURHOOD (the cycle-34 rule): everything else filed this cycle touches budgets, weather or the HUD message row. This one touches none of them.

The kanban-staleness-audit skill exists (.claude/skills/kanban-staleness-audit/) and has never been run over the historical sections -- it was built in cycle 34 after being named as missing three times, and then applied only to STILL REAL. Run it over the six oldest 'New this cycle' sections. The cycle-31 rule requires a file:line for every claim about current code; entries predating that rule have none, which is exactly what makes them unfalsifiable and why they rot.

ACCEPTANCE: each audited entry is either deleted, moved to Done with the commit that did it, or given the file:line that makes it checkable.

title: Cap the wave number's width in next_wave_note, or say the budget bounds it
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md, 'New this cycle (48)', third entry.

_budget_hud_message_row now measures Hud.next_wave_note(999, 9999, ...) (game/game.gd:2071) deliberately -- a budget is about what the FORMAT allows, not what the game is expected to reach. But next_wave_note (game/hud.gd:1505) formats the wave number with no width cap, so the budget's worst case is set by a digit count nothing in the code constrains. Endless mode has no wave ceiling, so 999 is a guess wearing a worst-case's clothes.

Either cap the formatted number (and assert the cap), or write in next_wave_note's own header that its width is bounded by the budget's chosen maximum and not by the format -- so the next person to widen it knows where the real limit lives.

ACCEPTANCE: a test that fails if the note can exceed the width the budget assumes.

title: Decide what rain pays, now that drought pays 150%
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md, 'New this cycle (48)', first entry -- direct consequence of closing -4c1l.

WaveDirector.seed_multiplier_for returns 1.5 for drought and 1.0 for everything else. Rain still heals pests (WEATHER_RAIN_HEAL_FRACTION) and pays base rate, so it is now the only weather with a downside and no compensation. A forecast the player reads has one weather they want and two they don't, which is a worse decision space than before the bonus existed.

Three shapes: rain pays a smaller bonus; rain gets a non-seed upside (faster regrowth, a free replant); or drought's bonus shrinks and rain's heal shrinks with it. NOTE the overlap with -oo7e (weather has no counter-play, blocked on the user): if weather gains a real counter, this rebalance is downstream of that decision and should not be done first.

ACCEPTANCE: every weather has at least one thing the player wants about it, named in next_wave_note before the wave commits.

title: Check that comments citing a verb or a test are still true
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (29 of 30)'. Measured this cycle: five comments in game/ name a devtools verb and ONE named a verb that does not exist (both commit_uproot headers claimed 'the devtools verbs' call it; list-commands --offline has nothing matching uproot). Nine comments name a test_* function, eight of which exist -- the ninth is test_selftest, a FILE name, which any checker must accept. Both classes are cheap to verify: list-commands --offline parses registrations with no game running, and test functions are a grep of test/. Build them as ONE 'comments that cite something' pass rather than two thin checkers; high precision, low volume, and this project leans hard on 'the alarm is test_X' as documentation.

title: Name every node the code keeps a reference to
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (28 of 30)'. 123 add_child calls in game/ against 93 .name assignments. The selection marker was in that gap: drawn on every selected plant, path @SelectionMarker@31, addressable from no test and no bridge command -- in a project whose OverlayScreen header says node paths are a contract. Not every anonymous node is a defect, but nothing distinguishes deliberate from overlooked. Derivable rule for a checker: a node that is add_child-ed AND stored in a member variable is one the code will refer to again, so a test or the bridge probably wants to as well.

title: Count hosted nodes that did not survive the test
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (27 of 30)'. _T.free_ui(host) runs at the end of every hosting test and a node that freed ITSELF in between is indistinguishable from one that did not. Counting what was hosted against what survives would have surfaced this cycle's defect as a warning on its first run, years of cycles earlier. Same caveat as the sibling bead: run_tests.gd is harness-owned, so this is an upstream proposal, but the measurement can be prototyped locally in a test first.

title: Refuse an equality assertion whose two sides are the same object
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (27 of 30)'. test_corn_shoots_the_pest_closest_to_escaping asserted target == far where BOTH were the same freed Pest, and passed for many cycles. run_tests.gd's [VACUOUS] catches a test that ran zero assertions; nothing catches one whose operands were both nothing. A cheap approximation: in _T.assert_eq (and assert_true on a bare ==), if both sides are Objects with the same instance id, that comparison cannot fail and is almost always a mistake -- report it the way [VACUOUS] is reported. Note this is a harness-side change (tools/run_tests.gd is regenerated by scaffold), so it belongs upstream rather than as a local edit.

title: Audit tests that name nodes after an await
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (26 of 30)'. test_corn_shoots_the_pest_closest_to_escaping (test/unit/test_combat.gd:288) builds two pests, hosts them, awaits instantiate_scene, and only THEN puts them in a typed array -- under harness 0.42.0 one is already freed by that point. Whether or not the harness caused it, that is the shape tools/settle_read_check.py exists to catch: a value read after settle frames that were still moving. Sweep every test that hosts nodes and then names them, and decide per case whether to re-fetch after the await or to assert the node survived.
close_reason: Guard added to _furthest_along_in_range (skips invalid entries; the doc names the tension with test signal). The audit found the real defect: the test's far pest was on the last leg of its route and freed itself during settle frames, so target == far compared two freed references and passed. Fixed and proven with a planted nearest-target implementation. No checker -- 9 candidates, 1 real; rule written into godot-test-isolation instead.

title: Guard _furthest_along_in_range against a stale pest
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (26 of 30)', found while bisecting the 0.42.0 regression. game/plant.gd:412 takes Array[Pest] and reads pest.global_position with no is_instance_valid check. Game builds that array fresh from the pests group every frame, so it is safe today by CONSTRUCTION rather than by contract -- and a targeting function that crashes on a stale entry is a crash in a shipped game rather than a failed assertion. The 0.42.0 crash dereferenced exactly this. Cheap: skip invalid entries, and the existing tests already pass arrays by hand so the guard is directly testable.
close_reason: Guard added to _furthest_along_in_range (skips invalid entries; the doc names the tension with test signal). The audit found the real defect: the test's far pest was on the last leg of its route and freed itself during settle frames, so target == far compared two freed references and passed. title: Assert the invariant, not the three instances

Register a project verb returning ProjectSettings.globalize_path('res://') plus the git branch, so any session can assert in one call that it is talking to its own build. Upstream fix filed as G-018; this is the local guard.
acceptance_criteria: cmd project_identity returns the absolute res:// path; a documented one-liner in CLAUDE.md compares it against the working directory before a runtime pass.
close_reason: project_identity verb reports project_root, user_dir, git branch/sha read from disk, worktree-aware; verified live against git rev-parse and offline discovery

title: Tint the threat level as it climbs
description: threat_level() renders as a small integer in the same cream as every other readout, so 'this wave is worse than the last' is something the player has to read and compare rather than see. Tint the threat portion of the wave label green -> amber -> red across the level range so the escalation is preattentive. The level is already a pure static function, so this is a colour lookup.
acceptance_criteria: A static Hud.threat_colour(level) with tests pinning the endpoints and monotonic movement between them; the label uses it.
close_reason: Wave readout tints cream->amber->red via static Hud.threat_color(), saturating at level 12; verified live at both ends

title: Placement preview should warn when a non-combat plant is road-adjacent
description: A hungry pest eats whatever plant is nearest and a Sunflower cannot fight back, but nothing on screen says 'this tile is one hungry mutation away from losing your economy plant'. PlacementPreview already computes reach and legality per cell, so this is nearly free now: road-adjacency is one is_path check on the four neighbours, and the preview is the node that would draw the warning. Only applies to plants with PlantCatalog.reach(id) == 0.0 -- a Corn Cobbler next to the road is fine, that is the point of it.
acceptance_criteria: Hovering a grass cell orthogonally adjacent to the road with the Sunflower selected draws a distinct warning cue; the same cell with a Corn Cobbler selected does not; both covered by unit tests.
close_reason: Closed

title: Per-run lane pressure for the end-of-run post-mortem
description: The lane pressure overlay now shows a whole wave's loss distribution, faded by one decay step per wave, which answers 'where did I lose this wave'. It cannot answer 'which cell has bled me all game'. Accumulate a second, never-faded tally alongside the per-wave one and show it on the end-of-run screen, so the post-mortem tells the player where their garden was actually weak.
acceptance_criteria: Board keeps a run-total pressure map separate from the decaying per-wave one; the end-of-run banner or screen renders it; a unit test shows the run map surviving fades that clear the wave map.
close_reason: Closed

title: Show a readable threat level for endless mode
description: Health, speed, count, gap and mutation chance now all climb independently past wave 8 and the player can see none of them -- the HUD just says 'Wave 39 / 8'. Derive one threat number (or a wave-start banner naming what went up this wave) from the five WaveDirector static functions, which are already pure and callable without a running wave. This is a readout, not a new system.
acceptance_criteria: A static WaveDirector.threat_for(wave) that is monotonic past the fixed table and constant inside it, shown on the HUD, with unit tests for both halves.
close_reason: Closed

title: A richer husk should rot faster, so sweep order becomes a decision
description: Husk size and glow now scale with value, but the timer does not: a 9-seed husk and a 2-seed one both rot in exactly CompostMeter.HUSK_LIFETIME (10s). Sweeping in any order is therefore optimal and the board asks nothing. Scale the lifetime inversely with value (a richer husk decays faster) so 'which one first?' is a real decision, and so the new size cue carries urgency as well as worth.
acceptance_criteria: drop_husk stores a per-husk lifetime derived from value; HuskLayer's rot ring reads that instead of the constant; a unit test shows a high-value husk expiring before a low-value one dropped at the same moment.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lane pressure should record every cell pests were lost at, not just the worst
description: Board.record_lane_pressure only ever receives the single furthest-reached cell for a wave (Game._wave_worst_cell), so a wave where pests died at scattered points along the lane only ever lights up the worst one. Recording every cell a pest died/escaped at (not just the max) would draw the whole 'where the damage happened' picture instead of one hot pixel.
close_reason: Closed

title: Endless mode should scale pest health/speed too
description: WaveDirector._endless_groups scales count/gap and mutation_chance_for scales mutation chance as endless mode runs longer, but Pest.SPECIES health/speed stay fixed forever -- a wave-60 pest is exactly as tough as a wave-9 one. Scale health and/or speed slightly past some endless threshold, mirroring the mutation-chance climb, so late-game pressure isn't pure quantity.
close_reason: Closed

title: Husk size/glow should scale with value
description: HuskLayer._draw() draws every husk at a fixed 9px radius regardless of CompostMeter's stored value, so a mutated pest's 1.5-2x husk_multiplier() payout is invisible until clicked. Scale the drawn radius (or ring brightness) by value so a bigger payout reads visually across the board, the way mutation tints already do for the pest itself.
close_reason: Closed

title: Second bite frame for a beetle's long chew
description: chomp_flower_eating.png is one fixed picture for the whole chew animation, aphid or beetle alike, even though a beetle's chew is 2.6s — long enough to read a second frame. Swap in an 'almost done' frame once chew_progress() > 0.6 (the same threshold the shrinking ring already reads) to sell 'big pests take a while' with just a second sprite and one if-check.
close_reason: chomp_flower_eating_late.png swaps in past chew_progress()>0.6 (LATE_BITE_THRESHOLD); verified headless (3 ChompFlower unit tests + sprite style contract) and live (texture path polled across a real slow-motion beetle chew, crossing exactly at 61%)

title: Endless mode should mutate faster over time
description: WaveDirector._endless_groups scales pest count and gap as endless mode continues, but MUTATION_CHANCE stays fixed at 40% forever, so wave 40 looks exactly as 'weird' as wave 8. Scale mutation chance upward (or widen MUTATIONS with a rarer fourth trait) past some endless-mode wave threshold so a long run keeps feeling different.
close_reason: WaveDirector.mutation_chance_for(wave) climbs by 0.02/wave past the fixed table, capped at 0.85; verified headless (4 unit tests) and live (curve sweep matching the exact formula shape)

title: Say in CLAUDE.md that list-commands has an offline mode
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (29 of 30)'. The verb table describes list-commands as runtime discovery for a launched session. Its --offline mode parses the registration sites statically with no game at all, which makes 'does a verb by this name exist' a free question -- that is what disproved a stale doc claim this cycle in one command. The harness section is regenerated by scaffold, so this note belongs in the project's own part of CLAUDE.md rather than inside the managed block.

title: Write down what 'armed' looks like, once
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (28 of 30)'. Two surfaces now show a pending destructive change and they use different second channels: a bullet mark on the Keys screen's rows, doubled line weight on the board's selection marker. Both are correct for their surface -- a Label and a draw_line shape have different vocabularies -- and together they mean the project has no single answer to 'what does armed look like', which is the kind of thing that drifts as surfaces are added. Write the pair down beside GardenTheme.DANGER so the third surface inherits a decision rather than inventing one.

title: Give Pest a last_survivable_leg() instead of re-deriving it by eye
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (27 of 30)'. Three test files build pests with hand-set _leg values against hand-written routes, and the relationship between 'a route of N points' and 'the last leg a pest can sit on without escaping' is _route.size() - 2, written down nowhere and re-derived by eye each time. Getting it wrong by one is exactly this cycle's bug. Either expose it on Pest or give the tests a helper that places a pest at a FRACTION of its route, so no test does the arithmetic.

title: Make verify_ledger stats show the suite count over time
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (26 of 30)'. The bisect that proved gh#43 rested on a suite count taken by hand before the install. .devtools/verify-runs.jsonl already records tests.total per run, so the history exists -- a stats line reading '552 for the last 12 runs, 0 this run' would surface a dependency regression without anyone remembering to take a before-measurement. Cheap, and it turns the ledger from a record into an alarm.

title: Check that every glyph the game draws exists in the font
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (24 of 30)'. A missing glyph renders as a .notdef box with a real width, so GardenTheme.measure() returns a plausible number, every width budget passes, and the only way this project has ever caught one is by looking at a screenshot. Font.has_char() exists. Worth pairing with the glyph table above: once every glyph is named in one place, asserting the font has all of them is a loop.

title: Mark which budget floors have actually been tested
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (23 of 30)'. hud_readouts (10px) and hud_stats_row (19px) earned their floors by being pushed through them in anger. hud_message_row's 40px is a number picked while declaring it, with 342px of headroom, and cmd budgets reports the two kinds identically -- so a floor that has never been approached looks exactly like one that has been defended. Either add a field saying so, or say it in the constant's comment; the goal is that a reader can tell a measured floor from a placeholder.

title: Say how much game is left, not just what is next
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (22 of 30)'. The last-wave note is the only place the game admits a run is nearly over. The prep strip, the wave counter and the threat number all describe the NEXT wave without ever saying how much is left. WaveDirector.WAVES.size() is static and current_wave is on every state dict, so '3 waves to go' is available everywhere and used nowhere. Endless has no answer, which is itself the interesting design question rather than a blocker.

title: Decide how a FIRST record is celebrated
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (20 of 30)'. The roll deliberately refuses when previous_best is 0: counting up from a zero the player never held is a lie. But a first-ever record is the most significant one they will set and currently gets LESS than a later, smaller one, which is backwards. The answer is a different treatment rather than a roll -- decide what, then build it. Filed as a decision, not as work.

title: Roll the seeds counter the way the record rolls
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (20 of 30)'. The seeds readout moves far more often than the record does. Hud._punch_readout already scales it on change, so 'this number moved' machinery exists and stops short of showing the movement -- a 45-seed purchase reads as a jump. Use the pattern from TitleScreen._arm_record_ratchet: a pure renderer, the final text set first, a restoring callback. Note the difference: seeds go DOWN as well as up, and a roll downward needs deciding rather than assuming.

title: Give kanban.md entries ids so their status can be derived too
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (19 of 30)'. kanban.md has the same shape log-devtools.md had: an entry's real status is whichever mention is newest, and cycles 34 and 36 each found a section whose heading said 'not filed yet' over entries that had shipped. A kanban_ledger sibling to gap_ledger.py is the obvious tool and cannot be written, because kanban entries have no ids to key on. The enabling change is small -- a [K-NNN] on each entry under the idea backlog -- and it is the prerequisite, not the tool.

title: Decide whether a drought should slow the non-shooters
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (18 of 30)'. Plant.fire_interval_scale is read by CornCobbler and Dandelion only; Chomp, Sundew and Sunflower pace themselves by other means (is_busy(), droplets, a growth gauge), so a drought slows two plants of five. That is arguably right -- a drought should hurt shooting, not chewing -- but it is an accident of which plants happen to read the multiplier rather than a decision anyone wrote down. Decide it, then either write the reasoning into Plant.fire_interval_scale's doc comment or extend it.

title: Pay more for surviving a wave under weather
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (17 of 30)'. SeedBank does not know weather exists, so surviving the hardest version of a wave pays exactly what the easy version pays. WaveDirector.threat_for() already exists and already rises monotonically -- it is the natural place to hang a payout multiplier, and doing it there rather than in SeedBank keeps 'how hard was that' in the one file that already answers it.
close_reason: Drought pays 150% on direct seed drops (WEATHER_DROUGHT_SEED_BONUS), named in next_wave_note and weather_note. Also corrected _budget_hud_message_row, which measured only plant names and not the prep note now widest on that row. bce07e5

title: Align the key column across the two screens that show keys
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (16 of 30)'. The pause card now right-aligns its keys against a gutter (game/pause_screen.gd:_build_key_list); KeyBindingScreen centres its RowKey%d labels in a fixed 140px column (game/key_binding_screen.gd:85), neither derived nor matching. Two screens showing the same eight keys in two different alignments is the kind of thing nobody reports and everybody notices. Do it after the shared measurement lands.

title: Widen the mirror gate to the other prose invariants
description: Source: cycle 32's step 5 reflection. tools/mirror_check.py compares ONE named block in TWO named files, and says so under NOT COVERED. The repo has other prose that must agree with something: the parallel-safe gate list in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md must name every tools/*_check.py that exists (it is hand-maintained and a new checker can be forgotten -- three were added in three cycles), and the harness section's verb table must not name a verb list-commands does not report. Both are derivable rather than hand-checkable, which is the derive-the-list shape. Low priority: no instance of either drifting yet, unlike the mirror, which had two.

title: Show the key hint on the HUD's own buttons
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (15 of 30)'. The HUD's 'Grow the next wave' button has a keyboard verb behind it and never says so -- a player who rebinds a key sees it only on the two screens that own bindings. Drawing the hint from KeyBindings.label_for() makes a rebinding visible where the player actually is. Depends on the legend column split: this would be the third surface to show key names, and the pause card just spent a cycle learning that a key name a player chose can be far wider than one we shipped.

title: Widen SHORT_NAMES to the keys the engine names badly
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (14 of 30)'. KeyBindings.SHORT_NAMES (game/key_bindings.gd:121) covers 8 of the ~100 bindable keys -- Esc, four arrows, Space, two Enters. Everything else falls through to the engine's own name, fine for F1 and poor for punctuation (KEY_BRACKETLEFT renders as something no player calls it). Do it with the derive-the-list recipe rather than one complaint at a time: derive the set the engine names badly, assert SHORT_NAMES covers exactly it, plant both directions.

title: Reuse SelectionMarker's pattern for a placement preview cue

The same pattern (corner brackets, dimmer/dashed) could show 'this is where the cursor would place a plant' before the click lands, reusing the exact node/technique instead of inventing a new cursor overlay concept.
